"The REAL victim of 9/11 was Mamdani's fake aunt?! We don't even know if she exists! He said she was to scared to wear her hijab on the subway after 9/11!" one anti-Mamdani protester told the crowd. "And let's talk about Islamophobia for a second! It is NOT irrational for me to fear them!" Trump to mark 9/11 's 25th anniversary at Pentagon President Donald Trump will Friday, honoring victims and first responders, while Vice President JD Vance commemorates the anniversary at the World Trade Center site alongside former Presidents Obama, Bush, and Clinton, plus former NYC Mayor Rudy Giuliani. | | ---|---|--- The White House will have officials present at all three attack sites, including Shanksville, Pennsylvania, marking Trump's continued pattern of attending Pentagon ceremonies during his presidency, as he did in 2017, 2019, and last year. Ahead of the anniversary, the Tunnel to Towers Foundation displayed a recovered World Trade Center steel beam at the White House as part of a cross-country tour; Trump, who witnessed the attacks from New York as a real estate developer, has previously described watching the towers from his office window. JD Vance ignites the RNC with chilling speech: He 's ready for 2028... Vice President JD Vance and enthusiastic crowd reactions at the GOP midterm convention's closing night, benefiting from a favorable speaking slot after Trump's Day 1 headliner and Marco Rubio's absence, though Vance urged focus on November first. Vance handled a protester waving a Mexican flag by turning it into a rallying moment, drawing praise from attendees who said the moment reinforced his presidential presence; he also urged disaffected conservatives frustrated over the Iran war not to abandon the party. Multiple attendees said they left convinced Vance is ready to be the party 's next leader, with some Republican officials calling his speech his best yet, even as Vance and Trump have both said it's too early to settle on a 2028 successor. Never Forget 25 years ago, radical Islamic terrorists attacked America in an attempt to scare us into submission and destroy all that is good in our country. While some have forgotten the horrors of that day, and have let the 3,000+ victims fade into distant memory, most Americans have refused to forget what happened, and have become defiant and unwavering in their love for our way of life and our values that created a beacon of hope and opportunity in the world for men to live free and determine their own destinies. Today we affirm that America is our home, and we are proud of it and we love it and we will defend it from all threats foreign and domestic. The most horrific act of terror cannot deter us, and evil will never prevail. Never forget, and God bless all the victims and their families on this day. \- The PolitiBrawl Editors You're currently a free subscriber to . I need you to hear this part just as clearly as you heard everything else.
The guardrails are holding. Not because they were built to hold under this kind of pressure. They weren't. They're holding because people are standing their ground.
Democracy Defenders Fund and Campaign Legal Center have filed lawsuits against Trump's 2025 and 2026 executive orders on voting. Twenty-four Democratic AGs joined together to block USPS restrictions on mail voting. They went to federal court in Massachusetts. They got a 14-day restraining order.
DOJ appealed all the way to the Supreme Court.
And lost.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..CyH1W292q-d3QhE-LG1w4bux7oDPaHwEm9l0GM_FEg0?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=214814476)
Read that again. They took it to SCOTUS. And the courts said no.
This is happening over and over. The bad guys are moving fast and they keep running into walls. Not because the walls were always there. Because people built them. Lawyers, organizers, attorneys general, advocates, voters who showed up and kept showing up.
I stood on those Capitol steps on January 6th. I've thought a lot about what it means to hold a line, to physically, literally hold a line when everything in you is saying move. That's what this moment is. That's what these lawsuits are. That's what showing up in November is.
They cannot win on policy. They know that. So they are trying to change who gets to vote. That's what's in front of us.
Sixty days.
You know what to do. Check your registration. Check the people around you. If you know anyone in Texas, have them check their status at votebeat.org/texas before October 5th. Share this. Talk about it. Don't let the news cycle bury it.
I'm in this with you every single day.
Together in the fight, Harry

A Chinese national with ties to Oklahoma was arrested in Maine on Wednesday and briefly held at the Penobscot County jail before he was transferred to a separate facility.
Terry Liu, aka Jia Jia Liu, of Calais, was transferred to an undisclosed facility Thursday afternoon pending a detention hearing for charges of theft of government property and destruction of government property, according to Penobscot County Jail records and court records.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/7ba3feba-1ab1-4b9e-a284-1c827b45041a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Court records show Liu has been charged with theft of government property and damaging government property.

Penobscot County Sheriff's records show Liu entered the jail at 9:51 am on Thursday morning but was then transferred to an undisclosed facility at 1:30 pm.
As of Thursday evening, court records showed he had a detention hearing Friday morning.
According to a Washington County source, Liu's Poole Street property in Calais -- located on the Canadian border -- was raided by what locals believed to be FBI agents on Thursday as well.
The source said Liu, who held a job as a customs officer at the Ferry Point Bridge, was apprehended at Bangor International Airport (BIA) trying to catch a flight back to China.
The Penobscot County Sheriffs Department declined to comment.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/8e1fd6a5-3e51-4387-8f7f-1e9c00519f49?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The Ferry Point International Bridge connects St. Stephen, New Brunswick, in Canada to Calais, across the St. Croix River.
According to county property records, Liu purchased property in Calais in 2018.
Before that he lived in Oklahoma, where his Facebook account indicates he attended college and worked in a government job.
Corporate records and licensing records show Liu briefly owned a cannabis license tied to Jliu Farm LLC based in Webbers Falls, Okla.

---|---|---
This would not be Washington County's first brush with international intrigue featuring cannabis entrepreneurs.
In 2024, three individuals believed to be non-citizens were arrested in Machias at a property owned by the Mass.-based HBA Properties: Ming Li (52), Dong Yang Li (60), and Peng You Phang (61).
They were charged with Illegal Cultivation of Marijuana and Unlawful Trafficking.
Due to the scale of the black-market infrastructure, the U.S. Department of Justice later moved to civilly seize the Machias property along with several other illicit grow houses across the state.

The Fed doesn't editorialize. It counts. And its own balance sheets just put a number on the greatest wealth hoard in human history -- parked inside America's "nonprofit" sector.
Every quarter, without fanfare, the Federal Reserve publishes the Z.1 -- the Financial Accounts of the United States. It is the dullest document in Washington and the most honest, because accountants don't do press releases. And in the latest Z.1 release, buried in the balance sheet for nonprofit organizations, is a number that should stop every American cold: $14.2 trillion in combined assets held by U.S. nonprofits -- $14.125 trillion as of the first quarter of this year, per the St. Louis Fed's own data feed, and climbing every quarter.
Sit with that for a second. That hoard is larger than the combined economies of Japan, Germany, and India -- three of the largest nations on Earth. It is larger than the annual output of every farmer, welder, coder, and trucker in America multiplied several times over. A "charitable" sector, by the Fed's own accounting, controls more wealth than almost every empire, monarchy, and trust fund ever assembled in the history of mankind.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/c81f43cc-bfb2-4f24-a512-1ae2be77ec59?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
And who built it? Not the Fed. Not Wall Street. Congress. Congress is the only institution on the planet in all of human history with the legal power to amass $14.2 trillion -- because it can take it from you, launder it through intermediaries, and call the residue "civil society."...

And in the latest Z.1 release, buried in the balance sheet for nonprofit organizations, is a number that should stop every American cold: $14.2 trillion in combined assets held by U.S. nonprofits -- $14.125 trillion as of the first quarter of this year, per the St. Louis Fed's own data feed, and climbing every quarter. Sit with that for a second. That hoard is larger than the combined economies of Japan, Germany, and India -- three of the largest nations on Earth. It is larger than the annual output of every farmer, welder, coder, and trucker in America multiplied several times over. A "charitable" sector, by the Fed's own accounting, controls more wealth than almost every empire, monarchy, and trust fund ever assembled in the history of mankind. | | ---|---|--- And who built it? Not the Fed. Not Wall Street. Congress. Congress is the only institution on the planet in all of human history with the legal power to amass $14.2 trillion -- because it can take it from you, launder it through intermediaries, and call the residue "civil society."... | | Peter, **Twenty-five years ago today, our nation faced an unimaginable tragedy that changed America forever.** On September 11, 2001, nearly 3,000 men, women, and children lost their lives in New York City, at the Pentagon, and in a field in Shanksville, Pennsylvania. _Today, we pause to honor the memory of those we lost and hold their families in our hearts._ **We also pay tribute to the incredible courage of our first responders—the firefighters, police officers, paramedics, and everyday citizens who ran toward danger to save others. Their selflessness reminds us of the true strength and resolve of the American spirit.**

| | In the aftermath of that dark day, our country united around a simple promise: **_Never Forget._** Today, as Americans, we renew that solemn pledge. We remember the lives taken, honor the heroes who served, and give thanks for the brave servicemen and women who continue to protect our freedom at home and abroad. **May God bless the families of the fallen and God bless the United States of America.** In remembrance, Russell Fry

| | **_Meet Russell:_** Born and raised in Surfside Beach, SC, Congressman Russell Fry is the proud and homegrown Representative for South Carolina’s 7th Congressional District. Growing up in a cinder block home with no heating or air conditioning, Russell learned at an early age that hard work and perseverance pave the only true path to the American Dream. He watched his parents work day in and day out to make ends meet. And the values they instilled in him during his upbringing led Russell to self-fund both his undergraduate education at the University of South Carolina, and later his law studies at the Charleston School of Law. At Charleston, Russell served as the President of the Student Bar Association and even helped the school achieve its American Bar Association accreditation. He went on to practice law in the Grand Strand area for over a decade before entering the political arena to serve in the South Carolina House of Representatives for State House District 106 (Horry County). During his seven-year tenure in the SC House, Russell fought to safeguard Constitutional liberties, lower taxes, and put the best interests of South Carolina families above all else. He climbed the ranks to become Chief Majority Whip, and also chaired the House Opioid Prevention Study Committee. Under Russell’s leadership, 18 policy initiatives to combat the opioid crisis were signed into law. Since the first day he stepped foot in Washington, Russell has strived to shake up the corrupt status quo and deliver real change for the American people. He believes adamantly that so long as the American people stand united, we can keep the American Dream alive for every citizen of our great nation. Russell is a dedicated husband to his wife, Bronwen, and a loving father to his son, James. The family lives in Murrells Inlet with their chocolate lab, Jasper.

name: Kirsten Gillibrand
subject: Today, we honor them.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Gillibrand for Senate
body:
Folks,

Twenty-five years ago today, nearly 3,000 people went to work and never came home. Since then, brave first responders and survivors have faced serious illnesses from the toxic exposure they endured at rescue sites.

Today is about remembering those we lost, and keeping our promise to the survivors: the first responders and the families who have been living with the weight of that day ever since.

I have spent my career fighting to make sure this country keeps its promise to those heroes and to make sure the World Trade Center Health Program is fully funded.

Politics continues to threaten the care these heroes depend on. It’s deeply unfortunate, but it’s why we have to keep pushing until this program is fully funded and permanently secured.

I am thinking today of the families still grappling with loss, the survivors still fighting for their health, and the first responders who gave everything and deserve everything in return.

25 years later, we continue to honor and remember them. And we will never stop fighting for them.

Keeping you close,
Kirsten Gillibrand

clean_body: Folks, Twenty-five years ago today, nearly 3,000 people went to work and never came home. Since then, brave first responders and survivors have faced serious illnesses from the toxic exposure they endured at rescue sites. Today is about remembering those we lost, and keeping our promise to the survivors: the first responders and the families who have been living with the weight of that day ever since. I have spent my career fighting to make sure this country keeps its promise to those heroes and to make sure the World Trade Center Health Program is fully funded. Politics continues to threaten the care these heroes depend on. It’s deeply unfortunate, but it’s why we have to keep pushing until this program is fully funded and permanently secured. I am thinking today of the families still grappling with loss, the survivors still fighting for their health, and the first responders who gave everything and deserve everything in return. 25 years later, we continue to honor and remember them. And we will never stop fighting for them. Keeping you close, Kirsten Gillibrand *

A crooked, melted, rusted steel beam rising from an inscribed black base on a suburban Maryland roadside -- the people who pass it every day carry the story. The most powerful memorials aren't always the biggest ones, and a town of 2,000 can hold a piece of Ground Zero -- it makes you want to pull the car over.
**A Beam on Connecticut Avenue**
Kensington, Maryland sits just inside the Capital Beltway, and its 9/11 memorial stands in front of Kensington Volunteer Fire Department Station 5 on Connecticut Avenue, where thousands of commuters pass it daily, many without slowing down.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/db0a56b8-e6cb-4a13-9bc1-72352a84f99c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The centerpiece is a sixteen-foot, one-ton box beam -- twisted, burned, and scarred -- recovered from the point of airplane impact at the World Trade Center. The plaque at its base reads: "This twisted and scarred piece of steel from the point of impact at the World Trade Center on September 11, 2001, memorializes the 2,976 persons lost that day in New York City, the Pentagon, and Shanksville, Pa. It also serves as an enduring testament to the American spirit. We shall never forget."
Nearby lies a shard of granite pulled from the Pentagon's point of impact -- and Kensington has a personal claim there: its volunteer firefighters responded to the Pentagon on the morning of the attack. The memorial park, dedicated in June 2011, was designed and built by the local construction community under the leadership of the late KVFD honorary member Stephan Heidenberger, championed by department president Steven Semler, and funded entirely through donations and volunteer labor. In 2019, the town added a plaque honoring the passengers and crew of Flight 93, making this small roadside park one of the only memorials anywhere to touch all three crash sites. Every September, the fire company holds a service beside the beam.
**The Great Dispersal**
Kensington's beam is one artifact of a largely forgotten chapter: after the recovery effort ended, Port Authority officials distributed World Trade Center steel to fire departments, towns, and universities that asked. The result is a decentralized national memorial landscape -- hundreds of sites, by some counts more than a thousand, most of them unlisted in any guidebook.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/42d4bdf8-7d97-4810-b13a-3e5d5d6cd5e6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**Napa 's Garden of Steel and Glass**
One of the best-kept secrets sits in California wine country. Downtown Napa -- better known for tasting rooms than tributes -- shelters the 9/11 Memorial Garden at 1040 Main Street, and it may be the most beautiful small 9/11 memorial in America.
The story begins when the Napa Fire Department was offered thirty tons of steel from the wreckage of the Twin Towers. The community turned to Gordon Huether, a Napa-based public artist with an international reputation, to lead what became a roughly $1 million public-private project. Huether secured six massive pieces of steel from both the north and south towers and composed them in a quiet walled garden rather than on a pedestal. Laminated glass panels, their inner layers printed with the names of the 2,997 people killed, stand among the beams; at dusk, soft lighting turns the whole ensemble into something closer to a cathedral than a roadside marker. Completed in 2013, it rewards a slow visit: run a hand along the mill-scale of a beam that once helped hold up Manhattan, then read names scrolling past in glass.
Where Kensington's memorial is raw -- iron twisted by violence, shown as it was found -- Napa's is contemplative, grief rendered as craft. Both approaches work; together they show the range of what communities have built.
Ten minutes south, Huether designed a companion piece in American Canyon: a steel collar cut from one of the towers' I-beams, elevated on two concrete supports between tall, illuminated glass panes. Two memorials, one valley -- a remarkable density of authentic WTC steel for a region 2,900 miles from ground zero.
**Elsewhere: A Geography of Remembrance**
California holds more understated gems. Laguna Beach's 'Semper Memento' stands in Heisler Park, where the Pacific provides the sound design. Cal Expo hosts a 9/11 Memorial Plaza in Sacramento; LAX built "Recovering Equilibrium" to honor the flight crews lost that morning; and every September, Pepperdine University's Heroes Garden in Malibu blooms with an American flag for each victim -- nearly three thousand of them on a hillside above the sea.
The heartland has its own quiet inventory. Green Township, Ohio, centers its memorial on a striking twelve-foot length of World Trade Center steel in a peaceful reflection park. Boston's Logan Airport, departure point for two of the hijacked flights, commissioned a luminous glass memorial for those aboard.
The impulse crossed oceans. In Ringfinnan, near Kinsale in County Cork, Ireland, a garden of remembrance honors the 343 FDNY firefighters who died -- the work of Kathleen Cait Murphy, a Kinsale native who spent forty years nursing in New York and counted Fr. Mychal Judge, the chaplain who died first that morning, among her friends. And in Jerusalem's Arazim Valley stands the 9/11 Living Memorial, dedicated in 2009 -- the most comprehensive memorial outside the United States, inscribed with every victim's name.
One last footnote the memorials themselves record: the arithmetic of loss keeps shifting. Kensington's plaque counts 2,976; Napa's glass lists 2,997; the national memorial in New York inscribes 2,983, including those killed in the 1993 bombing. The numbers differ because the questions differ -- who counts, counted when, from where. Each memorial froze its own honest answer in steel, stone, or glass.
**Why the Small Ones Matter**
The famous memorials -- the reflecting pools, the Pentagon's cantilevered benches, the field in Shanksville -- are national acts of mourning. The small ones are local acts of love, built by volunteer fire companies and wine-town artists, tended by garden clubs, passed by commuters who mostly don't look. And then, one September morning every year, they do. That may be the healthiest thing about American memory of 9/11: twenty-five years on, remembrance hasn't been concentrated in one place. It's been dispersed, like the steel itself, into thousands of ordinary towns -- waiting quietly by the road.

name: Elissa Slotkin
subject: Remembering September 11, 25 years later
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY ELISSA SLOTKIN FOR MICHIGAN
body:
#

Dear friend -
Most of us remember exactly where we were on September 11th, 2001 when we heard the U.S. had been attacked. We remember what we were doing and who we were with. It was a generational event, like Pearl Harbor or the Kennedy assassination. It’s hard to overstate the way the attacks changed our country forever. And for thousands of us, it defined a generation.
I was in New York City on 9/11. I had just started graduate school. I still remember the sound of F-16s over New York; the smell of clouds of dust and smoke; and the sound of sirens from every fire and police station as they headed towards the towers. By the time the smoke cleared, I knew what I wanted to do with my life — I wanted to go into national security. Within a year, I was recruited by the CIA. And within my first year at Langley, I was sent on my first of three tours in Iraq alongside the military.
Every year, we remember those we’ve lost and the bravery of our first responders who ran toward the danger as the rest of us ran away. I think about those images of ash-covered fire trucks, with no one left to drive them. And I remember so vividly in the months afterwards the constant playing of bagpipes as yet another fire or police officer's remains were laid to rest.
I also find myself focusing on something else from the days and weeks afterwards: the sense of unity across the country that emerged out of the rubble. The shared sense of purpose, unlike I have felt before or since. The feeling that we as Americans were on the same team.
In those early months, we certainly weren't perfect. Muslim-Americans and immigrants were targeted. And the events of 9/11 kicked off an era of significant errors in wars far from home that we’re still grappling with today. But, in our imperfect way, Americans were embodying the idea that while we are very different, and we have lots of difficulties, we love this country and we want it to be a better place.
25 years later, I choose to believe we can be that country again. But at a time when our country feels so divided and that unity can feel so far away, I hope that we’ll all take a minute out of our busy lives, step back, and share our memories with our kids or grandkids: the bravery that our first responders demonstrated, and the resilience and patriotism that communities across our country showed in coming together.
We are still that country. We are on the same team. I refuse to believe that our politics will feel like this forever. And I’m so grateful I got to experience our country united, so I know what we’re aiming to get back to.
Sincerely,
Elissa

P.O. Box 4145
East Lansing, MI 48826

---|---|---
A Chinese national who managed to get a job working as a U.S. Customs and Border Protection supervisor in Calais has been arrested and charged in what FBI agents claim was a plot to install modified hardware in Department of Homeland Security computers.
Terry "Jiajia" Liu -- originally of Guangzhou, per his Facebook page -- was arrested after a counter intelligence investigation captured hidden-camera footage of him breaking into government computers and modifying the hard drives.
According to court records released Friday in Maine District Court, Liu is alleged to have stripped valuable components from government computers, replaced them with inferior parts and traded the originals to an electronics retailer for credit.
Liu, 39, is charged with theft and damage of government property in a case involving 46 altered computers at three Maine border facilities. Prosecutors are seeking to keep him jailed, citing frequent international travel, financial resources and a home close enough to Canada that an ankle monitor might not prevent him from leaving the country.

The alleged scheme persisted after a port director explicitly warned Liu not to move computers or their parts. Investigators later installed cameras that, according to an FBI affidavit, captured the supervisor opening government computers and swapping components during overnight shifts.
The affidavit doesn't state or imply that the alternative hardware the Chinese national installed on Homeland Security computers might have served an espionage purpose.
The government estimates that restoring the altered parts would cost $20,460. Replacing all 46 computers would cost an estimated $105,800, before additional expenses to configure them for government use.
Liu appeared Thursday before U.S. Magistrate Judge John C. Nivison in Bangor, where he was ordered temporarily held without bail pending a detention hearing scheduled for Friday morning. He waived a preliminary hearing but requested a hearing on the government's detention motion.
According to FBI Special Agent Christopher J. White's affidavit, Liu was a CBP supervisor assigned to the Calais Port of Entry, with responsibilities extending to Ferry Point and Milltown. His job included limited information-technology duties, but he was not authorized to modify computers.
On March 18, 2025, Port Director Theodore Cummings put that restriction in writing after speaking with Liu.
"Please do not move any computers or computer parts," Cummings wrote.
The email distinguished equipment maintained by a contractor from CBP computers, which were to be serviced by the agency's information-technology personnel.
"I do appreciate the intent but we should stay in our lane and report deficiencies through the work ticket process," Cummings wrote.
Months later, CBP personnel discovered that approximately 23 computers had been modified without authorization. Original processors, memory and hard drives had been replaced with components that did not meet agency requirements. Many of the machines had been reconnected to the CBP network.
A subsequent inventory expanded the total to 46 computers: 38 at Calais, six at Ferry Point and two at Milltown.
[Share The Robinson Report](https://substack..628-1XR3DzDeZUHBcv0Csibype0gMeR9AQ1K0d8qTsI?)
Thirty-nine had undergone processor replacements, six had memory changes and eight had hard-drive changes, according to the affidavit. Some machines had more than one type of modification.
The government computers were equipped with 14th-generation Intel processors. Investigators found that many had been fitted instead with older processors or Intel Pentium models. Other machines had less memory or storage than their original configurations.
Investigators also found a potential route for the missing parts: Newegg's trade-in program.
The affidavit describes 13 emails Liu sent from a personal account to his official CBP email address containing shipping labels and trade-in summaries for processors matching the model missing from government computers. The offers were for $200 or $210 apiece.
Records obtained from Newegg showed that Liu received credit for trading in 14th-generation Intel Core i7 processors 16 times between May 2025 and July 2026, according to the FBI. Investigators also identified three $200 Newegg credits in his American Express records.
The criminal complaint charges Liu with stealing 10 Intel processors worth more than $1,000 between approximately May 2025 and January 2026. A second count alleges that he damaged or attempted to damage CBP computers between January and March 2026, causing more than $1,000 in damage or attempted damage.
Investigators' account includes a detailed reconstruction of Liu's movements during a January 9 overnight shift.
Shortly after midnight, he allegedly carried computers into a training room, removed their side panels and began working on the components. A camera installed days earlier recorded him using what appeared to be a screwdriver, removing a processor and scraping its surface in a manner consistent with removing thermal paste, White wrote.
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=2246936&post_id=215228574&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjE1MjI4NTc0LCJpYXQiOjE3ODkxMzY1MzksImV4cCI6MTc5MTcyODUzOSwiaXNzIjoicHViLTIyNDY5MzYiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.RWV0cF9YSbzZ-1iK0EA8zn2p_LtJmBK4ljpwg4DlXWc)
Liu then allegedly installed a replacement processor, moved components between machines and connected monitors, keyboards and network cables to test the computers.
At one point, investigators said, he appeared to use his government identification to log into a modified computer.
Another camera, installed above Liu's assigned desk in March, allegedly recorded him removing a memory module from a computer and placing it in his desk drawer. He then carried the computer into a server room and connected it to a monitor, keyboard, mouse and network cable.
The affidavit describes working conditions that could leave Liu separated from other officers. During midnight shifts, one supervisor typically covered the open ports in the area. Traffic at the Calais facility was directed to the cargo side, while Liu's assigned desk was on the passenger side.
According to White, Liu admitted during a September 9 interview that he replaced CBP components with older parts purchased from Amazon and Newegg and used government parts to obtain trade-in credit.
His explanation changed during the interview, the agent wrote.
Liu initially said he made the modifications to improve the computers' efficiency. Under further questioning, according to the affidavit, he acknowledged knowing that the changes degraded performance and said he acted because he was angry about how long CBP computer repairs took.
[Share The Robinson Report](https://substack..628-1XR3DzDeZUHBcv0Csibype0gMeR9AQ1K0d8qTsI?)
In seeking detention, Assistant U.S. Attorney Chris Ruge argued that Liu had engaged in "recent and frequent international travel" and had "apparent foreign connections and substantial means with which to flee."
Ruge also argued that the allegations against Liu could weaken his ties to his government employer and the United States.
His residence near the Canadian border offered "significant opportunity" to leave the court's jurisdiction even under location monitoring, the prosecutor wrote.
Liu's immigration status is unclear. Though he has described himself as a native of Guangzhou, China, he has also posted images to Facebook suggesting that he voted in the 2020 election.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/1e1d7cfb-27de-4103-a75b-8d7f01fbea06?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Although investigators say modified computers were reconnected to the agency's network, the affidavit does not allege that Liu installed malware or transmitted government information to anyone outside the agency.
Newegg is an online retailer, founded by Taiwanese billionaire Fred Chang, specializing in computer components, electronics and gaming equipment. Its trade-in program lets customers exchange eligible used processors, memory and graphics cards for credit toward new purchases.
According to a Washington County source, Liu's Poole Street property in Calais was raided by what locals believed to be FBI agents on Thursday.
Liu purchased that property in 2018, according to property records.
Before that he lived in Oklahoma, where his Facebook account indicates he attended college and worked in a government job.
Corporate records and licensing records show Liu briefly owned a cannabis license tied to Jliu Farm LLC based in Webbers Falls, Okla.
The source said Liu was apprehended at Bangor International Airport (BIA) trying to catch a flight back to China, though the court records do not confirm the nature of his apprehension.

More details are emerging regarding the arrest of Terry Liu, a federal employee the FBI claims illegally accessed and modified government computers. Sep 11 | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- A Chinese national who managed to get a job working as a U.S. Customs and Border Protection supervisor in Calais has been arrested and charged in what FBI agents claim was a plot to install modified hardware in Department of Homeland Security computers. Terry "Jiajia" Liu -- originally of Guangzhou, per his Facebook page -- was arrested after a counter intelligence investigation captured hidden-camera footage of him breaking into government computers and modifying the hard drives. According to court records released Friday in Maine District Court, Liu is alleged to have stripped valuable components from government computers, replaced them with inferior parts and traded the originals to an electronics retailer for credit. Liu, 39, is charged with theft and damage of government property in a case involving 46 altered computers at three Maine border facilities. Prosecutors are seeking to keep him jailed, citing frequent international travel, financial resources and a home close enough to Canada that an ankle monitor might not prevent him from leaving the country. Hear it first. Sign up for The Robinson Report. | Terry Liu Fbi Affidavit962KB ∙ PDF file ---|--- | The alleged scheme persisted after a port director explicitly warned Liu not to move computers or their parts. Investigators later installed cameras that, according to an FBI affidavit, captured the supervisor opening government computers and swapping components during overnight shifts. The affidavit doesn't state or imply that the alternative hardware the Chinese national installed on Homeland Security computers might have served an espionage purpose. The government estimates that restoring the altered parts would cost $20,460. Replacing all 46 computers would cost an estimated $105,800, before additional expenses to configure them for government use. Liu appeared Thursday before U.S. Magistrate Judge John C. Nivison in Bangor, where he was ordered temporarily held without bail pending a detention hearing scheduled for Friday morning. He waived a preliminary hearing but requested a hearing on the government's detention motion. According to FBI Special Agent Christopher J. White's affidavit, Liu was a CBP supervisor assigned to the Calais Port of Entry, with responsibilities extending to Ferry Point and Milltown. His job included limited information-technology duties, but he was not authorized to modify computers. On March 18, 2025, Port Director Theodore Cummings put that restriction in writing after speaking with Liu. "Please do not move any computers or computer parts," Cummings wrote. The email distinguished equipment maintained by a contractor from CBP computers, which were to be serviced by the agency's information-technology personnel. "I do appreciate the intent but we should stay in our lane and report deficiencies through the work ticket process," Cummings wrote. Months later, CBP personnel discovered that approximately 23 computers had been modified without authorization. Original processors, memory and hard drives had been replaced with components that did not meet agency requirements. Many of the machines had been reconnected to the CBP network. A subsequent inventory expanded the total to 46 computers: 38 at Calais, six at Ferry Point and two at Milltown. ? Thirty-nine had undergone processor replacements, six had memory changes and eight had hard-drive changes, according to the affidavit. Some machines had more than one type of modification. The government computers were equipped with 14th-generation Intel processors. Investigators found that many had been fitted instead with older processors or Intel Pentium models. Other machines had less memory or storage than their original configurations. Investigators also found a potential route for the missing parts: Newegg's trade-in program. The affidavit describes 13 emails Liu sent from a personal account to his official CBP email address containing shipping labels and trade-in summaries for processors matching the model missing from government computers. The offers were for $200 or $210 apiece. Records obtained from Newegg showed that Liu received credit for trading in 14th-generation Intel Core i7 processors 16 times between May 2025 and July 2026, according to the FBI. Investigators also identified three $200 Newegg credits in his American Express records. The criminal complaint charges Liu with stealing 10 Intel processors worth more than $1,000 between approximately May 2025 and January 2026. A second count alleges that he damaged or attempted to damage CBP computers between January and March 2026, causing more than $1,000 in damage or attempted damage. Investigators' account includes a detailed reconstruction of Liu's movements during a January 9 overnight shift. Shortly after midnight, he allegedly carried computers into a training room, removed their side panels and began working on the components. A camera installed days earlier recorded him using what appeared to be a screwdriver, removing a processor and scraping its surface in a manner consistent with removing thermal paste, White wrote. Liu then allegedly installed a replacement processor, moved components between machines and connected monitors, keyboards and network cables to test the computers. At one point, investigators said, he appeared to use his government identification to log into a modified computer. Another camera, installed above Liu's assigned desk in March, allegedly recorded him removing a memory module from a computer and placing it in his desk drawer. He then carried the computer into a server room and connected it to a monitor, keyboard, mouse and network cable. The affidavit describes working conditions that could leave Liu separated from other officers. During midnight shifts, one supervisor typically covered the open ports in the area. Traffic at the Calais facility was directed to the cargo side, while Liu's assigned desk was on the passenger side. According to White, Liu admitted during a September 9 interview that he replaced CBP components with older parts purchased from Amazon and Newegg and used government parts to obtain trade-in credit. His explanation changed during the interview, the agent wrote. Liu initially said he made the modifications to improve the computers' efficiency. Under further questioning, according to the affidavit, he acknowledged knowing that the changes degraded performance and said he acted because he was angry about how long CBP computer repairs took. ? In seeking detention, Assistant U.S. Attorney Chris Ruge argued that Liu had engaged in "recent and frequent international travel" and had "apparent foreign connections and substantial means with which to flee." Ruge also argued that the allegations against Liu could weaken his ties to his government employer and the United States. His residence near the Canadian border offered "significant opportunity" to leave the court's jurisdiction even under location monitoring, the prosecutor wrote. Liu's immigration status is unclear. Though he has described himself as a native of Guangzhou, China, he has also posted images to Facebook suggesting that he voted in the 2020 election. | | ---|---|--- Although investigators say modified computers were reconnected to the agency's network, the affidavit does not allege that Liu installed malware or transmitted government information to anyone outside the agency. Newegg is an online retailer, founded by Taiwanese billionaire Fred Chang, specializing in computer components, electronics and gaming equipment. Its trade-in program lets customers exchange eligible used processors, memory and graphics cards for credit toward new purchases. According to a Washington County source, Liu's Poole Street property in Calais was raided by what locals believed to be FBI agents on Thursday. Liu purchased that property in 2018, according to property records. Before that he lived in Oklahoma, where his Facebook account indicates he attended college and worked in a government job. Corporate records and licensing records show Liu briefly owned a cannabis license tied to Jliu Farm LLC based in Webbers Falls, Okla. The source said Liu was apprehended at Bangor International Airport (BIA) trying to catch a flight back to China, though the court records do not confirm the nature of his apprehension. Later today I will join the Palo Alto community in rededicating a [memorial to Michael Ferugio](https://substack.com/redirect/224073c1-e572-4e61-9ca7-744e84cf51ac?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), one of our own who died when terrorists attacked our country on September 11, 2001 in New York City.
The loss of Michael means that at birthdays and holidays, the big milestones, the small moments - there has been an empty chair at his family's table.
But that deep, private loss belongs to all of us. Our community and our country.
I remember exactly where I was when the attack began 25 years ago. I'm going to admit my age here. I was in 7th grade. But it's like it was yesterday. Health class. The TV was on. And the rest of the day, this big, horrible thing grew and grew as we began to grapple with what had just happened.
Our country found strength and resolve after the attacks. We knew that divided we fall, but united we stand.
Today those words have a different meaning. They bring a different kind of grief, because today we are a different country.
The elites encourage us to hate our fellow Americans. They tell us our own neighbors despise our country and want to see its downfall - just because they are registered to vote under a different political party.
When will we remember who we are? Americans, not members of a political party. One nation, under God - indivisible. Capable of standing together in the face of great evil.
That's what I want us to remember when we tell each other to never forget.
Never forget that we lost people like Michael. 2,977 Michaels.
Never forget the extraordinary bravery of Americans that day, especially our firefighters. Ordinary people did extraordinary things, putting their own lives at risk to save their fellow Americans.
And never forget the way we came together. Candlelight vigils. [All of Congress](https://substack.com/redirect/fe307012-8e8d-4900-8c8c-10ec31d6ed83?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) singing God Bless America on the Capitol steps. Two of my classmates painted a mural at D.H.H. Lengel Middle School. I can still picture it today. [Let's Roll](https://substack.com/redirect/8fd7e7bf-af8d-45e6-ac72-df406d8ebdb4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), it says.
That's how we can honor Michael. That's how we can honor this 25th anniversary. By coming back together. In grief. In love. In community. And moving forward together.
Never forget.

body:
25 years ago this morning, 40 passengers and crew members boarded United Airlines Flight 93 expecting an ordinary flight across the country.

| | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/pPfeEsLFrJ4?e=63ab67bb25&c2id=8377c90e3583a614e646f5b9492ea9fd)
| | | | | | Peter,
25 years ago this morning, 40 passengers and crew members boarded United Airlines Flight 93 expecting an ordinary flight across the country.
Then the world changed.
After terrorists seized the plane, passengers called their loved ones and learned that planes had already struck the World Trade Center and the Pentagon.
Among those aboard was 32-year-old Todd Beamer—a husband, a father of two, with another child on the way.
Unable to reach his family, Todd was connected by phone with operator Lisa Jefferson. He told her that he and several other passengers planned to fight back. Before they did, Todd asked her to pray with him.
Then she heard him turn to the others:
“Are you guys ready? Okay. Let’s roll.”
Minutes later, Flight 93 crashed into a field near Shanksville, Pennsylvania.Forty ordinary people, confronted with an unimaginable choice, summoned extraordinary courage. They could not know whether they could save themselves. They only knew they might still save others.
So they acted.
For those of us who wore our nation’s uniform, September 11 carries another weight.I served for 30 years in the Army Reserve, including deployments overseas after 9/11. I had the privilege of serving alongside men and women who left their families and their lives at home because their country called. Some returned bearing wounds seen and unseen.
Some never returned at all.
Their service was part of what followed September 11. But the first acts of defiance happened that very morning in the stairwells of burning buildings, among first responders rushing toward danger, and aboard an airplane over Pennsylvania.
Twenty-five years later, millions of Americans were not yet born when the towers fell, the Pentagon burned, or Flight 93 came down in that field.
That makes our responsibility to remember greater, not smaller.
We must tell them about the 2,977 innocent people we lost. We must tell them about the first responders. We must tell them about those who answered the call to serve.And here in Pennsylvania, we have a special responsibility to tell them about Todd Beamer and the 39 other passengers and crew members of Flight 93.
They had only minutes to decide what they would do with the time they had left.
They chose courage. They chose sacrifice. They chose others before themselves.
That field near Shanksville is hallowed ground because of that choice.
Twenty-five years later, Pennsylvania remains the keeper of their story. May we always be worthy of that responsibility.
May God bless the heroes of Flight 93, all those we lost on September 11, their families, our first responders, and every American who answered the call to serve.
We will never forget.
\- Stacy

Honoring the bravery, sacrifice, and enduring spirit of America
[](https://emails.teapartypatriots.org/CL0/https:%2F%2Fwww.teapartypatriots.org/1/010001a090e36501-975910d1-6ec0-4b64-804e-977a02f7241e-000000/tnz3QFJRCtvqTwBveB2BYe7wCAep32_z88SsFSejUcA=452)Patriot–On September 11, 2001, our nation changed forever.We all remember where we were the moment the world stood still. We remember the heartbreak, the grief, and the innocence lost on that crisp September morning.**But we also remember what rose from the ashes.** We remember the unmatched bravery of hundreds of firefighters, law enforcement officers, and emergency personnel who courageously ran directly into danger to save total strangers.We remember the heroes aboard Flight 93 who sacrificed everything to shield our nation’s capital.**Most of all, we remember the overwhelming sense of unity that bound us together as Americans in the dark days that followed.** On September 12th, there were no political divisions or party lines – there were only neighbors helping neighbors, flags proudly displayed on every doorstep, and a unified pledge to protect the land of the free.To the families who still carry the heavy burden of a missing loved one, to the first responders who continue to fight long-term illnesses, and to the brave service members who stepped up to defend our freedom in the years following – you are in our prayers.**May God bless the memories of those we lost, comfort their families, and forever bless the United States of America.** With deep gratitude and solemn remembrance,Jenny Beth Martin _This email list is a joint venture of the following separate organizations: Tea Party Patriots Action, Inc., Tea Party Patriots Foundation, and Tea Party Patriots Citizens Fund. **Friday, September 11, 2026**
We shall not forget. We remember the smoke, the noise, and the sudden, shattering silence. But we also remember the tables that became sanctuaries. We remember the families who clung to one another in the quiet, finding the strength to endure the unthinkable.
Resilience is not always a shout; often, it is the quiet decision to keep the home warm and the table set. We honor the fallen by protecting the peace they left behind.
In the silence of this day, we find our footing. We remember why we fight.

**Pause. Breathe. Look Deeper.**
**Refuel.**
**Welcome to Sweet Ground.**

Friend, Today, let's take a moment to remember the innocent lives lost twenty-five years ago on September 11, 2001, and to honor the extraordinary courage of the first responders who ran toward danger on the day the world stopped. For many of us, the events of that day remain vivid—the shock, the uncertainty, and the profound grief that rippled across the country. But we also remember the days that followed, when fear was met with an uncommon resilience, and _neighbors took care of neighbors_ simply because it was the right thing to do. That spirit of service and community is something we carry forward every day here in Tennessee. It's in the quiet commitment of our firefighters, our law enforcement officers, our healthcare workers, and _everyday people who show up for one another in times of need._ Today, let’s keep the victims, the survivors, and the families who still carry the weight of that loss in our thoughts and prayers. We will never forget, and we honor their sacrifice by working every day to fulfill the promise of America. In solemn remembrance, Jerri Green
Democratic Nominee for Tennessee Governor

Thirty-five generations ago, my ancestors built lives in the high desert of New Mexico. Growing up fishing with my dad and running through the desert with my cousins, I fell in love with New Mexico’s natural wonders and learned that we all have a responsibility to care for our planet.
_Since my childhood, I have seen the impacts of climate change on New Mexico._
That’s why, when I was elected to Congress, I fought to protect sacred lands. As Secretary of the Interior, I helped protect more land and water than any administration in U.S. history while also creating good jobs in clean energy and conservation and cleaning up legacy pollution.
**But now all of that progress is at risk.**

In Operation ENDURING FREEDOM, I served alongside Muslim American airmen who loved this country enough to defend it while some of their countrymen back home faced horrifying bigotry and questioned whether they belonged.
And every American who came home from that war owes a debt to the Afghan interpreters and partners who made our survival and the success of our mission possible.
They guided our troops through terrain and language and danger we could never have navigated alone.
They did it knowing the Taliban would hunt down them and their families for it and they bravely chose us anyway.
We promised them safety.
Instead, this cruel administration is deporting them back to Afghanistan to face certain death, trading the lives of proven friends for one more round of Islamophobic theater.

**Friday, September 11, 2026 -**_**** Ansarallah seizes Yemen's Red Sea coast to Bab al-Mandab. Saudi forces launch two airstrikes on Yemen's Mocha airport. * * *
# Yemen
* **Ansarallah seizes Yemen 's Red Sea coast to Bab al-Mandab: **Ansarallah (also known as Houthi) forces swept through the remaining stretch of Yemen's Red Sea coast in an 18-hour offensive, securing the coastline from Mocha south to the Bab al-Mandab Strait, according to Al Jazeera.
* Saudi-backed Yemeni forces completely withdrew from the area following the battle of Al-Waziyah, west of Taiz, and the Ansarallah capture of the Khalid ibn al-Walid military base. With government forces abandoning Mocha, Ansarallah fighters encountered little resistance as they advanced south, taking Dhubab and then Murad, the last coastal town held by government forces.
* Ansarallah naval forces subsequently moved offshore, seizing Mayyun Island (also known as Perim) in the Bab al-Mandab Strait two miles off Yemen's west coast and advancing into Zuqar Island, where fighting is ongoing.
* **Saudi forces launch two airstrikes on Yemen 's Mocha airport: **Saudi military forces [carried out](https://substack.com/redirect/3b752f03-56a6-451b-ad8f-95e2a2c15c61?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) two airstrikes on Mocha airport in western Yemen, the Ansarallah-affiliated Al-Masirah reported, following the Ansarallah takeover of Mocha. Six missiles also targeted the port in Mocha, according to AFP.
* **Pumping station on Saudi 's critical East-West oil pipeline reportedly struck: **Satellite imagery [showed](https://substack.com/redirect/57f24983-b412-4e37-9a02-110bb097ab65?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) plumes of smoke near Saudi Arabia's critical East-West oil pipeline early Friday, while NASA's fire-monitoring system detected fires in the area, amid reports that Yemen's Ansarallah targeted a pumping station along the pipeline. Saudi authorities have not yet announced an incident at the site.
* The East-West Pipeline has become increasingly important since the outbreak of the U.S.-Iran war, allowing Saudi Aramco to move crude from the kingdom's eastern oil fields to the Red Sea and bypass the Strait of Hormuz.
* **Axios: Trump declined Saudi requests to strike Ansarallah as they advanced:** Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman [called](https://substack.com/redirect/926295b3-ff8b-40f0-a17e-7663d28ce918?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) U.S. President Donald Trump twice on Thursday, urging him to launch strikes against Yemen's Ansarallah as they advanced along the Red Sea coast toward Bab al-Mandab, two U.S. officials told Axios. Trump declined, with Washington saying it has no plans to intervene directly for now.
* A senior Trump administration official said Washington was focused on ensuring "freedom of navigation in the Red Sea" while "empowering our regional partners to take the lead."
* More than 100 U.S. military advisers are [providing](https://substack.com/redirect/ffc6d78d-1c6d-46a5-8165-b7578edee117?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) intelligence and targeting support to Saudi Arabia's military campaign against Ansarallah through a newly established joint forces command, according to a new report from CNN, with one official putting the total closer to 200 troops.
* **Six districts captured in operation against Saudi-backed forces in western Yemen, Ansarallah says:** Ansarallah [said](https://substack.com/redirect/5c54530e-4225-4d41-b719-e51c7d88d93e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Friday that the group had taken control of six districts across Taiz and Hodeidah governorates, covering some 5,400 square kilometers, during a large-scale military operation launched on September 3 to expel Saudi-backed forces from parts of Yemen's western coast.
* Military spokesperson Yahya Saree said the operation came amid a 12-year Saudi assault and blockade on Yemen, aimed at pressuring the country over its demands and its support for the Palestinian people, with attacks intensifying in recent months.
* "The armed forces affirm that maritime navigation is safe for all companies, with the exception of Saudi ships," Saree said, adding that operations would continue under an equation of "siege for siege" and "escalation for escalation" until "the aggression is stopped and the blockade on our people is lifted."
* **IOM: At least 46,000 displaced in Yemen as fighting escalates:** At least 46,000 people have been displaced across Yemen's West Coast and Taiz governorate since fighting escalated last week, the International Organization for Migration (IOM) [said](https://substack.com/redirect/ac3da660-6d7c-4b46-92c5-a8104f375ca5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Friday, warning that the number is "alarmingly rising by the hour." On Tuesday, the UN agency had put the number at around 18,500.
* Entire villages have reportedly emptied in Maqbanah, Jabal Habashi, and al-Ma'afer as fighting moved closer to populated areas, while large numbers fled Mocha overnight. Displaced people are arriving in Lahj and Aden, with others moving north toward Ibb. The key Mocha-Taiz road has also reportedly been cut.
* IOM said it temporarily suspended all operational movements on Friday because of the deteriorating security situation, while emergency stocks have already been depleted following the recent flood response.
* For Drop Site, Carolina Pedrazzi and a reporter in Yemen spoke to families in the Jabal Zaid displaced persons camp--some of whom were facing their second or third displacement. **[Read the piece here](https://substack.com/redirect/01728082-04a5-4300-b71a-32f9d5ca0e3c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).**
* **Iranian officials praise Ansarallah advances along Yemen 's Red Sea coast: **Senior Iranian officials praised Ansarallah's rapid advance along Yemen's Red Sea coastline.
* Iranian Vice President Mohammad Reza Aref [hailed](https://substack.com/redirect/4ef51b84-a3a4-40de-8787-fa0b880327b1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the "victories of the heroic nation of Yemen." Mohammad Mokhber, an adviser to Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei, [congratulated](https://substack.com/redirect/76e61e76-ae63-4b37-8b37-83338592af15?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Ansarallah on what he called a "resounding victory." "Iran's might in the Strait of Hormuz and the homegrown resolve of the resistance have driven the US and its allies into a tactical and strategic impasse," Mokhber said.
* Iran's Foreign Ministry called for an end to Saudi Arabia's blockade of Yemen and an immediate return to negotiations between Saudi Arabia and Ansarallah.

# Iran
* **IRGC says it destroyed U.S. unmanned vessel at entrance to Strait of Hormuz:** Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy [said](https://substack.com/redirect/eaf5ce3c-c14d-4d40-9784-d6c02405be78?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Thursday that it struck and destroyed a U.S. unmanned surface vessel, a "Saildrone Explorer-type," at the entrance to the Strait of Hormuz, Iran's Mehr News Agency reported.
* In its statement, the IRGC Navy said it targeted the vessel and "foiled its aggressive mission," claiming the U.S. military had recently deployed unmanned vessels to the Strait to avoid directly confronting Iranian forces.
* Since March 2025, Saildrone and Palantir have partnered on AI-powered autonomous maritime surveillance.
* **Oil climbs above $108 as U.S. diesel prices hit record high:** Oil prices continued to climb on Friday, with Brent crude futures rising $1.05, or 1%, to $108.68 a barrel, after surging more than 6% on Thursday.
* In the U.S., the average price of diesel reached a record $6.06 a gallon on Friday, surpassing $6 for the first time, according to AAA data cited by AFP. The rise comes in the wake of increasing attacks along key shipping routes in the Middle East.
* **South Korea, Iran discuss Strait of Hormuz:** South Korean Foreign Minister Cho Hyun and Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi discussed developments and navigation through the Strait of Hormuz in a phone call on Friday, according to Seoul's Foreign Ministry.
* Cho expressed concern over the regional situation and reiterated South Korea's support for free and safe navigation through the strait. The two agreed to maintain communication.
* The call came after Seoul dispatched an inspection team to assess a potential deployment of South Korean troops to the region at the behest of the U.S.
* **Satellite images indicate likely oil slicks near Strait of Hormuz after U.S. attack on tankers:** Satellite images from the European Copernicus programme [show](https://substack.com/redirect/ee6d7608-7beb-47db-acf7-038041647a56?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) what experts say are likely oil slicks off Iran's coast, east of the Strait of Hormuz, following U.S. attacks that sank oil tankers in the area, AFP reported.
* Images taken Wednesday and Thursday show long brownish streaks on the water around 20 kilometers off the Iranian coast, near coral reefs designated as wetlands of international importance.
* Two of the tracks begin at locations where the tankers Kylo and Riesco transmitted their last signals before being sunk on September 5 and 8, respectively. The U.S. military said Tuesday that it had destroyed five tankers in the Gulf of Oman in response to Iranian ballistic missile attacks on a U.S. warship.
* **Vance secretly called military commanders directly for unfiltered Iran war assessments** : Vice President JD Vance made an unusual effort over the spring and summer to [call](https://substack.com/redirect/5b3af9e2-79c1-434e-bfb5-bfc673c27027?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) U.S. military commanders across the Middle East, Europe, and Asia directly, seeking unvarnished assessments of the Iran war, according to a Thursday report from The New York Times.
* Commanders told Vance their stockpiles of Patriot interceptors, Army Tactical Missile Systems, and Precision Strike Missiles were at their lowest levels ever, with one theater down to fewer than 100 Patriots by late spring, prompting Vance to develop deep private concerns about the war's strategy that contrasted sharply with Trump's continued public claims that the U.S. had "already won the war" and faces no supply problems.

# Palestine
* **Israeli drone strike kills Palestinian, wounds nine in southern Gaza:** A Palestinian was killed and nine others, including children, were wounded on Friday when an Israeli drone [struck](https://substack.com/redirect/f30c7c79-fe2b-4797-9e49-6a66ede62173?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a group of people in the Al-Mawasi area of Khan Younis, southern Gaza, according to WAFA.
* **Nine Palestinians killed in Israeli attacks across Gaza on Thursday:** An Israeli drone struck a vehicle north of Khan Younis, killing one Palestinian. Another drone strike targeted a group of Palestinians in the Al-Qubba area of Al-Mawasi, killing three and wounding five.
* Another Israeli strike killed a Palestinian family, including two children, as they slept in Beit Lahia in northern Gaza: Momen Ahmad, his wife, Haneen Saleh, and their two daughters, sisters Lana, 12, and Bana, 8.
* The family had repaired two rooms in the middle of their partially destroyed home and were living there when it was struck. No one survived.
* Residents spent hours trying to recover the family from beneath the rubble as Israeli forces continued firing toward the area. "We managed to recover three bodies. There is also a little girl--we managed to recover part of her body, but the rest is still under the rubble," a relative, Zuhair Al-Haisami, told Drop Site's Mohamed Ahmed.
* **Watch the dispatch from Mohamed Ahmed[ here](https://substack.com/redirect/ef3d82c0-9a6e-4470-a043-38915f9f09aa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).**
* A ninth Palestinian died from wounds sustained in an Israeli strike on Al-Mawasi, north of Khan Younis, earlier in the day.
* **Israel kills Hamas 's Qassam Brigades Khan Younis commander: **Hamas's armed wing, Al-Qassam Brigades, confirmed Friday that Israel killed Mohammed Al-Yazouri, a member of its General Military Council and commander of its Khan Younis brigade, in a strike Thursday, describing it as a "cowardly Israeli assassination operation."
* The Israeli military claimed the strike killed a company commander and another member of the Khan Younis brigade.
* Israel signed a ceasefire agreement with Hamas on October 9, 2025, and has since killed 1,359 Palestinians and wounded more than 4,570 in Gaza.
* **Israeli forces, settlers carry out attacks and arrests across occupied West Bank:** Israeli forces detained around 30 Palestinians on Thursday, including two journalists and a former prisoner, during raids in several areas of the occupied West Bank.
* **Nablus:** Israeli settlers, accompanied by Israeli soldiers, [attacked](https://substack.com/redirect/345ba77e-ac72-4812-a95b-8fb755fd6e0e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Palestinian homes in the Al-Dhahra and Al-Hara Al-Tahta areas of Beita on Friday morning and stole a number of sheep, according to WAFA.
* **Tubas:** Settlers attacked a thyme crop belonging to a Palestinian farmer in the northern Yarza community, east of Tubas, on Thursday, removing and stealing a fence and destroying irrigation networks supplying the crop.
* **Somaliland offers to deploy 2,000 troops for Gaza stabilization force** : Somaliland President Abdirahman Mohamed Abdullahi [said](https://substack.com/redirect/4c989a7e-96f4-4b07-8238-ab11ad66489b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Wednesday the breakaway Somali region--recently recognized by Israel--is willing to deploy 2,000 troops for the planned U.S.-led International Stabilization Force (ISF) in Gaza, but is waiting for a formal request from Washington or Israel, according to The New Arab.
* Speaking at the MEAD conference in Washington, Abdullahi said his forces, which include an army of about 25,000 soldiers and a 1,500-person coast guard, are "ready" to contribute to the unit, which under Trump's Gaza plan would secure areas following an Israeli withdrawal, train Palestinian police, and support aid delivery.
* Last month, Uganda became the first African state to join the ISF, a move that sparked domestic debate over whether Kampala acted without African Union consultation.
* **Israeli soldiers detail "calculated mass killing" of Palestinians in new documentary:** A new documentary by Israeli co-directors Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor which premiered at the Venice Film Festival features interviews with 24 Israeli military intelligence officers and soldiers about "Israel's calculated mass killing of Palestinian civilians in Gaza," according to the film's synopsis. The film is titled "NAZA," a reference to an Israeli military acronym for civilian casualties, including men, women and children.
* "Interviewees describe hacking little girls' phones to see when their fathers came home and then bombing their houses, listening while the people on the line screamed and pleaded for help, while mothers cried over their burning daughters," Vulture [reported](https://substack.com/redirect/e143a3e3-96d8-4b64-8fd0-5b3b32fe8966?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Another officer recalls blowing up a building with 500 people in it to go after one target. All of the soldiers spoke on condition of anonymity and their appearance and voices were digitally altered.
* The film builds on previous reporting published by +972 Magazine, Local Call, and The Guardian. At a press conference following the premiere, Szor also reminded everyone that Palestinian journalists have reported on these facts.

# Lebanon
* **Israel detonates 1,100 tons of explosives at Ali Al-Taher ridge, blast registers like 4.2-magnitude earthquake:** The Israeli military [detonated](https://substack.com/redirect/f921f13e-e17d-479e-8e95-6cccb1667fbf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) 1,100 tons of explosives beneath the Ali Taher Ridge on the outskirts of Nabatieh Al-Fawqa in Nabatieh, southern Lebanon on Thursday night, claiming to have destroyed an underground complex belonging to Hezbollah, The Times of Israel reported.
* Seismic waves from the explosion [recorded](https://substack.com/redirect/619bdb5b-d6e0-4236-bd74-a282ce1e1bad?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) at 9:08 p.m. were comparable to a magnitude-4.2 earthquake, Lebanon's National Center for Geophysics said.
* The Israeli military said it would "reorganize" its deployment but continue to occupy the Ali Al-Taher Ridge through surveillance and firepower. The Israeli Army Radio reported Friday that Israeli forces have withdrawn from the Ridge to rear lines in the Shaqif area.
* The force of the explosion [sent](https://substack.com/redirect/719d4b92-2ed7-40d9-81c0-2e8bf282304a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) rocks and debris onto the Khiam-Marjayoun road, leaving it completely blocked on Friday, according to NNA. Residents of several villages in the Marjayoun district also [appealed](https://substack.com/redirect/d20dbea1-be6f-4539-82ec-8517a59d68a4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for water supplies after dust and debris from the blast covered homes, roads, and vehicles.
* **Israel continues attacks across other districts in southern Lebanon:**
* **Tyre (Sour):** Israeli forces carried out airstrikes, artillery shelling, and large-scale demolitions in Mansouri, including [blowing up](https://substack.com/redirect/dcd771bd-de74-4532-a4f6-7e581f142df7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) most of the town's public school. Two consecutive airstrikes [targeted](https://substack.com/redirect/5995cbbe-13d6-4ed4-8230-61cb5eb093cf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) infrastructure and residential neighborhoods, according to NNA.
* **Marjayoun:** Israeli forces moved into the Wadi Al-Jamal area on the northern outskirts of Meiss Al-Jabal, accompanied by artillery shelling that targeted a house and machine-gun fire in the area.

# U.S. News
* **Republicans blindsided by Trump 's $5,000 check pledge, sources say**: Key congressional Republicans, including Senate Majority Leader **John Thune** , were not [briefed](https://substack.com/redirect/dfab536d-c2fc-4a26-9876-c5efd118822f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) before President Donald Trump's Wednesday pledge to send $5,000 checks to every American adult if Republicans hold Congress, according to more than a dozen lawmakers and aides cited by NOTUS.
* GOP Rep. **Chip Roy** criticized the plan on social media, saying "dependency is evil & soul-sucking in all its forms," and a senior Senate Republican aide told the outlet flatly "it's not going to happen," citing inflation concerns and the estimated $1.2 trillion cost, or 3.5% of GDP.
* **GOP election officials from seven states urge Supreme Court to block Trump 's mail voting rule:** Republican chief election officials from seven states, including Georgia's **Brad Raffensperger** and Kansas's **Scott Schwab** , [filed](https://substack.com/redirect/ab519b7f-f1f9-4efc-9ecc-eb72a895187b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a brief Wednesday urging the Supreme Court not to let Trump's mail-in ballot order take effect before the November midterms, saying it's too late to implement it responsibly.
* The officials, alongside numerous current and former local election authorities, said: "attempting to implement the rule now will almost certainly lead to mistakes, delays and confusion for both voters and election officials."
* Trump signed the order in March, and it was formalized in an August U.S. Postal Service rule allowing the service to withhold ballot delivery from states that don't submit voter eligibility lists.
* A preliminary injunction from a Boston federal judge currently blocks the order from taking effect before November. On Thursday, the First Circuit Court of Appeals denied the Trump administration's request to lift this injunction, ruling in a nine-page opinion that the administration failed to show the rule wouldn't cause "chaos and widespread voter disenfranchisement."
* **Supreme Court blocks Trump-backed Missouri congressional map for November** : The U.S. Supreme Court once again [prevented](https://substack.com/redirect/08995b7e-3fe8-4a1e-82de-6f6698a1b31a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Missouri from using its Republican-redrawn congressional map for the November election, marking the second time this week the justices have weighed in on the state's chaotic redistricting fight.
* Missouri Secretary of State **Denny Hoskins** said his office would direct local election authorities to use the 2022 congressional map, which would position Democrats to retain their Kansas City-area seat.
* The reversal followed a whiplash sequence in which Justice **Brett Kavanaugh** initially deferred to Missouri's Supreme Court favoring the old map, only for federal Judge **Stephen R. Clark** to rule hours later that the new GOP-drawn map should be used to avoid "wreaking havoc" on election fairness, prompting state officials to briefly follow Clark's ruling, before it was appealed back to the Supreme Court.
* It remains unresolved how officials will reconcile using a different map in the general election than the GOP-redrawn map used to nominate candidates in August's primary.
* **Appeals court deals ICE ninth straight loss on mass detention policy:** The 4th Circuit Court of Appeals [ruled](https://substack.com/redirect/5dbce8a5-90dd-4420-a93b-15a1633af18d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) 2-1 Thursday against ICE's policy of detaining immigrants living inside the U.S. for years without bond, ICE's ninth straight loss at the federal appellate court level, with Judge**Nicole Berner** comparing the approach to the "historical stain" of Japanese internment during World War II.
* Nine of the 11 appellate circuits to consider the issue have now found the administration misread a 1996 immigration law that established deportation and detention policies, and which prior administrations interpreted as making detention mandatory only for people who had recently crossed the border.
* ICE abandoned this interpretation in July 2025 in favor of treating even longtime U.S. residents as "seeking admission" and subject to detention without bond.
* **Former EPA officials warn data center boom poses growing public health threat** : A group representing more than 800 former EPA employees [released](https://substack.com/redirect/f266e86c-a2c7-4fb6-98a2-e5b437da7a41?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a report warning that Trump administration policies weakening pollution safeguards and speeding data center approvals threaten to worsen health risks.
* The report, from the Environmental Protection Network, cites academic modeling which projects that data center air pollution could contribute to roughly 600,000 asthma cases, 1,300 premature deaths, and more than $20 billion in annual public health costs by 2028.
* It also lists 30 federal actions it says will increase pollution risks, including easing restrictions on diesel generators and off-grid gas plants and proposing to let developers begin construction before air pollution permits are approved.
* Former EPA enforcement official **Larry Starfield** noted the agency's staffing is at a four-decade low, leaving it ill-equipped to monitor or enforce pollution limits at the scale of the data center buildout, and UC Riverside professor **Shaolei Ren** , who led the report's underlying analysis, warned "the actual impact could be worse than we modeled" given the administration's explicit push toward increasing the use of fossil fuels.
