# Other International News
* **Putin, Xi, Pezeshkian arrive in New Delhi for BRICS summit:** Russian President Vladimir Putin [arrived](https://substack.com/redirect/42901057-9bd0-4161-a4df-653d43cece2d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in New Delhi Friday ahead of an 11-member BRICS summit expected to be dominated by the wars in the Middle East and Ukraine, joined by Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian for his first visit to India as president and Chinese President Xi Jinping for his first India visit since 2019.
* The ongoing war in Iran and the Gulf is expected to be the central fault line in the meeting, given the recent addition of several Gulf monarchies to the bloc, including Saudi Arabia and the UAE, and the body's recent failure to agree on a joint statement concerning the war in May.
* India, which maintains ties with both Iran and Israel while balancing relations with Washington, has turned increasingly to Russian oil amid the Iran-driven energy crisis, even as its foreign minister recently visited Kyiv and Zelenskyy thanked India for its "commitment to ending this unjust war."
* **Peru joins U.S. Shield of the Americas anti-cartel coalition:** President Keiko Fujimori [announced](https://substack.com/redirect/e20b0f3b-38ec-42a2-9ace-a6967d1d3900?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that Peru will join the U.S.-led "Shield of the Americas" coalition against drug cartels during Secretary of State Marco Rubio's visit on Thursday.
* Fujimori said Peru's participation would speed intelligence-sharing and joint action against transnational criminal groups, citing her country's experience fighting the Shining Path insurgency.
* Rubio's visit, part of a three-country Latin American tour also covering Ecuador and Colombia, built on existing defense ties between the countries, including Peru's January designation as a major non-NATO ally and a possible $1.5 billion U.S. military sale approved by Rubio, which would upgrade Peru's Callao Naval Base.
* Peru is also seeking relief from 12.5% U.S. tariffs imposed in July that have hit its blueberry, grape, and avocado exports. China continues to outpace the U.S. in bilateral trade with Peru, with Peru-China trade up 35% in the first half of the year compared to a 20% rise with the U.S. Rubio's Thursday visit prompted China's embassy in Lima to preemptively declare that "the Western Hemisphere is not anyone's 'backyard.'"
* **Fire kills at least 29 people, mostly students, in DRC 's rebel-held Bukavu:** A fire that [broke out](https://substack.com/redirect/8785f5ed-374f-42c0-b6d6-1c10fbd3782d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in the Chimpunda neighborhood of Bukavu, capital of the eastern DRC's South Kivu province, killed at least 29 people, including 19 girls and five boys, after spreading to two local schools and about 300 wooden homes, according to an AFC/M23 rebel spokesperson.
* Another local official said the fire was "followed by a violent stampede that forced students to trample over one another or look for a dangerous way out," with many fainting or losing consciousness during the chaos.
* Bukavu has been controlled since February 2025 by the Rwanda-backed AFC/M23 movement. Thursday's fire is one of several that have recently blazed through the city, including one last Sunday that destroyed more than 45 houses.
* **Ukrainian drone attacks kill two, wound seven in Russia 's Belgorod region**: Ukrainian drone attacks on Russia's Belgorod border region [killed](https://substack.com/redirect/4ad56766-0c24-47db-9f5e-46130b47fbf4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) two people and wounded seven Thursday, according to regional authorities.
* One man was killed when a drone detonated at an unnamed facility in Novy Oskol, injuring five others in various locations, while a second man was killed and a woman injured when a drone struck their car in Shebekino, near the Ukrainian border.
* **International Energy Agency cuts forecast on Russian oil production after Ukraine attacks:** The International Energy Agency has [lowered](https://substack.com/redirect/794344fe-d0cd-4c61-817b-908cb7163e44?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) its forecast for Russian oil production as Ukrainian drone strikes continue to damage refineries and other energy infrastructure.
* The agency cut its 2026 forecast by 125,000 barrels per day to 8.7 million bpd and reduced its 2027 projection by 235,000 bpd to 8.6 million bpd.
* The decline comes as Moscow itself has downgraded its 2026 production forecast to a 17-year low and lowered its fuel-export projections for both 2026 and 2027 because of the war which has increasingly seen Ukraine targeting refineries and other energy production facilities inside Russia.

This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday - Friday Yemen Ansarallah seizes Yemen 's Red Sea coast to Bab al-Mandab: Ansarallah (also known as Houthi) forces swept through the remaining stretch of Yemen's Red Sea coast in an 18-hour offensive, securing the coastline from Mocha south to the Bab al-Mandab Strait, according to Al Jazeera. Saudi-backed Yemeni forces completely withdrew from the area following the battle of Al-Waziyah, west of Taiz, and the Ansarallah capture of the Khalid ibn al-Walid military base. With government forces abandoning Mocha, Ansarallah fighters encountered little resistance as they advanced south, taking Dhubab and then Murad, the last coastal town held by government forces. Ansarallah naval forces subsequently moved offshore, seizing Mayyun Island (also known as Perim) in the Bab al-Mandab Strait two miles off Yemen's west coast and advancing into Zuqar Island, where fighting is ongoing. Saudi forces launch two airstrikes on Yemen 's Mocha airport: Saudi military forces two airstrikes on Mocha airport in western Yemen, the Ansarallah-affiliated Al-Masirah reported, following the Ansarallah takeover of Mocha. Six missiles also targeted the port in Mocha, according to AFP. Pumping station on Saudi 's critical East-West oil pipeline reportedly struck: Satellite imagery plumes of smoke near Saudi Arabia's critical East-West oil pipeline early Friday, while NASA's fire-monitoring system detected fires in the area, amid reports that Yemen's Ansarallah targeted a pumping station along the pipeline. Saudi authorities have not yet announced an incident at the site. The East-West Pipeline has become increasingly important since the outbreak of the U.S.-Iran war, allowing Saudi Aramco to move crude from the kingdom's eastern oil fields to the Red Sea and bypass the Strait of Hormuz. Axios: Trump declined Saudi requests to strike Ansarallah as they advanced: Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman U.S. President Donald Trump twice on Thursday, urging him to launch strikes against Yemen's Ansarallah as they advanced along the Red Sea coast toward Bab al-Mandab, two U.S. officials told Axios. Trump declined, with Washington saying it has no plans to intervene directly for now. A senior Trump administration official said Washington was focused on ensuring "freedom of navigation in the Red Sea" while "empowering our regional partners to take the lead." More than 100 U.S. military advisers are intelligence and targeting support to Saudi Arabia's military campaign against Ansarallah through a newly established joint forces command, according to a new report from CNN, with one official putting the total closer to 200 troops. Six districts captured in operation against Saudi-backed forces in western Yemen, Ansarallah says: Ansarallah Friday that the group had taken control of six districts across Taiz and Hodeidah governorates, covering some 5,400 square kilometers, during a large-scale military operation launched on September 3 to expel Saudi-backed forces from parts of Yemen's western coast. Military spokesperson Yahya Saree said the operation came amid a 12-year Saudi assault and blockade on Yemen, aimed at pressuring the country over its demands and its support for the Palestinian people, with attacks intensifying in recent months. "The armed forces affirm that maritime navigation is safe for all companies, with the exception of Saudi ships," Saree said, adding that operations would continue under an equation of "siege for siege" and "escalation for escalation" until "the aggression is stopped and the blockade on our people is lifted." IOM: At least 46,000 displaced in Yemen as fighting escalates: At least 46,000 people have been displaced across Yemen's West Coast and Taiz governorate since fighting escalated last week, the International Organization for Migration (IOM) Friday, warning that the number is "alarmingly rising by the hour." On Tuesday, the UN agency had put the number at around 18,500. Entire villages have reportedly emptied in Maqbanah, Jabal Habashi, and al-Ma'afer as fighting moved closer to populated areas, while large numbers fled Mocha overnight. Displaced people are arriving in Lahj and Aden, with others moving north toward Ibb. The key Mocha-Taiz road has also reportedly been cut. IOM said it temporarily suspended all operational movements on Friday because of the deteriorating security situation, while emergency stocks have already been depleted following the recent flood response. For Drop Site, Carolina Pedrazzi and a reporter in Yemen spoke to families in the Jabal Zaid displaced persons camp--some of whom were facing their second or third displacement. . Iranian officials praise Ansarallah advances along Yemen 's Red Sea coast: Senior Iranian officials praised Ansarallah's rapid advance along Yemen's Red Sea coastline. Iranian Vice President Mohammad Reza Aref the "victories of the heroic nation of Yemen." Mohammad Mokhber, an adviser to Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei, Ansarallah on what he called a "resounding victory." "Iran's might in the Strait of Hormuz and the homegrown resolve of the resistance have driven the US and its allies into a tactical and strategic impasse," Mokhber said. Iran's Foreign Ministry called for an end to Saudi Arabia's blockade of Yemen and an immediate return to negotiations between Saudi Arabia and Ansarallah. Iran IRGC says it destroyed U.S. unmanned vessel at entrance to Strait of Hormuz: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy Thursday that it struck and destroyed a U.S. unmanned surface vessel, a "Saildrone Explorer-type," at the entrance to the Strait of Hormuz, Iran's Mehr News Agency reported. In its statement, the IRGC Navy said it targeted the vessel and "foiled its aggressive mission," claiming the U.S. military had recently deployed unmanned vessels to the Strait to avoid directly confronting Iranian forces. Since March 2025, Saildrone and Palantir have partnered on AI-powered autonomous maritime surveillance. Oil climbs above $108 as U.S. diesel prices hit record high: Oil prices continued to climb on Friday, with Brent crude futures rising $1.05, or 1%, to $108.68 a barrel, after surging more than 6% on Thursday. In the U.S., the average price of diesel reached a record $6.06 a gallon on Friday, surpassing $6 for the first time, according to AAA data cited by AFP. The rise comes in the wake of increasing attacks along key shipping routes in the Middle East. South Korea, Iran discuss Strait of Hormuz: South Korean Foreign Minister Cho Hyun and Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi discussed developments and navigation through the Strait of Hormuz in a phone call on Friday, according to Seoul's Foreign Ministry. Cho expressed concern over the regional situation and reiterated South Korea's support for free and safe navigation through the strait. The two agreed to maintain communication. The call came after Seoul dispatched an inspection team to assess a potential deployment of South Korean troops to the region at the behest of the U.S. Satellite images indicate likely oil slicks near Strait of Hormuz after U.S. attack on tankers: Satellite images from the European Copernicus programme what experts say are likely oil slicks off Iran's coast, east of the Strait of Hormuz, following U.S. attacks that sank oil tankers in the area, AFP reported. Images taken Wednesday and Thursday show long brownish streaks on the water around 20 kilometers off the Iranian coast, near coral reefs designated as wetlands of international importance. Two of the tracks begin at locations where the tankers Kylo and Riesco transmitted their last signals before being sunk on September 5 and 8, respectively. The U.S. military said Tuesday that it had destroyed five tankers in the Gulf of Oman in response to Iranian ballistic missile attacks on a U.S. warship. Vance secretly called military commanders directly for unfiltered Iran war assessments : Vice President JD Vance made an unusual effort over the spring and summer to U.S. military commanders across the Middle East, Europe, and Asia directly, seeking unvarnished assessments of the Iran war, according to a Thursday report from The New York Times. Commanders told Vance their stockpiles of Patriot interceptors, Army Tactical Missile Systems, and Precision Strike Missiles were at their lowest levels ever, with one theater down to fewer than 100 Patriots by late spring, prompting Vance to develop deep private concerns about the war's strategy that contrasted sharply with Trump's continued public claims that the U.S. had "already won the war" and faces no supply problems. Palestine Israeli drone strike kills Palestinian, wounds nine in southern Gaza: A Palestinian was killed and nine others, including children, were wounded on Friday when an Israeli drone a group of people in the Al-Mawasi area of Khan Younis, southern Gaza, according to WAFA. Nine Palestinians killed in Israeli attacks across Gaza on Thursday: An Israeli drone struck a vehicle north of Khan Younis, killing one Palestinian. Another drone strike targeted a group of Palestinians in the Al-Qubba area of Al-Mawasi, killing three and wounding five. Another Israeli strike killed a Palestinian family, including two children, as they slept in Beit Lahia in northern Gaza: Momen Ahmad, his wife, Haneen Saleh, and their two daughters, sisters Lana, 12, and Bana, 8. The family had repaired two rooms in the middle of their partially destroyed home and were living there when it was struck. No one survived. Residents spent hours trying to recover the family from beneath the rubble as Israeli forces continued firing toward the area. "We managed to recover three bodies. There is also a little girl--we managed to recover part of her body, but the rest is still under the rubble," a relative, Zuhair Al-Haisami, told Drop Site's Mohamed Ahmed. Watch the dispatch from Mohamed Ahmed. A ninth Palestinian died from wounds sustained in an Israeli strike on Al-Mawasi, north of Khan Younis, earlier in the day. Israel kills Hamas 's Qassam Brigades Khan Younis commander: Hamas's armed wing, Al-Qassam Brigades, confirmed Friday that Israel killed Mohammed Al-Yazouri, a member of its General Military Council and commander of its Khan Younis brigade, in a strike Thursday, describing it as a "cowardly Israeli assassination operation." The Israeli military claimed the strike killed a company commander and another member of the Khan Younis brigade. Israel signed a ceasefire agreement with Hamas on October 9, 2025, and has since killed 1,359 Palestinians and wounded more than 4,570 in Gaza. Israeli forces, settlers carry out attacks and arrests across occupied West Bank: Israeli forces detained around 30 Palestinians on Thursday, including two journalists and a former prisoner, during raids in several areas of the occupied West Bank. Nablus: Israeli settlers, accompanied by Israeli soldiers, Palestinian homes in the Al-Dhahra and Al-Hara Al-Tahta areas of Beita on Friday morning and stole a number of sheep, according to WAFA. Tubas: Settlers attacked a thyme crop belonging to a Palestinian farmer in the northern Yarza community, east of Tubas, on Thursday, removing and stealing a fence and destroying irrigation networks supplying the crop. Somaliland offers to deploy 2,000 troops for Gaza stabilization force : Somaliland President Abdirahman Mohamed Abdullahi Wednesday the breakaway Somali region--recently recognized by Israel--is willing to deploy 2,000 troops for the planned U.S.-led International Stabilization Force (ISF) in Gaza, but is waiting for a formal request from Washington or Israel, according to The New Arab. Speaking at the MEAD conference in Washington, Abdullahi said his forces, which include an army of about 25,000 soldiers and a 1,500-person coast guard, are "ready" to contribute to the unit, which under Trump's Gaza plan would secure areas following an Israeli withdrawal, train Palestinian police, and support aid delivery. Last month, Uganda became the first African state to join the ISF, a move that sparked domestic debate over whether Kampala acted without African Union consultation. Israeli soldiers detail "calculated mass killing" of Palestinians in new documentary: A new documentary by Israeli co-directors Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor which premiered at the Venice Film Festival features interviews with 24 Israeli military intelligence officers and soldiers about "Israel's calculated mass killing of Palestinian civilians in Gaza," according to the film's synopsis. The film is titled "NAZA," a reference to an Israeli military acronym for civilian casualties, including men, women and children. "Interviewees describe hacking little girls' phones to see when their fathers came home and then bombing their houses, listening while the people on the line screamed and pleaded for help, while mothers cried over their burning daughters," Vulture . Another officer recalls blowing up a building with 500 people in it to go after one target. All of the soldiers spoke on condition of anonymity and their appearance and voices were digitally altered. The film builds on previous reporting published by +972 Magazine, Local Call, and The Guardian. At a press conference following the premiere, Szor also reminded everyone that Palestinian journalists have reported on these facts. Lebanon Israel detonates 1,100 tons of explosives at Ali Al-Taher ridge, blast registers like 4.2-magnitude earthquake: The Israeli military 1,100 tons of explosives beneath the Ali Taher Ridge on the outskirts of Nabatieh Al-Fawqa in Nabatieh, southern Lebanon on Thursday night, claiming to have destroyed an underground complex belonging to Hezbollah, The Times of Israel reported. Seismic waves from the explosion at 9:08 p.m. were comparable to a magnitude-4.2 earthquake, Lebanon's National Center for Geophysics said. The Israeli military said it would "reorganize" its deployment but continue to occupy the Ali Al-Taher Ridge through surveillance and firepower. The Israeli Army Radio reported Friday that Israeli forces have withdrawn from the Ridge to rear lines in the Shaqif area. The force of the explosion rocks and debris onto the Khiam-Marjayoun road, leaving it completely blocked on Friday, according to NNA. Residents of several villages in the Marjayoun district also for water supplies after dust and debris from the blast covered homes, roads, and vehicles. Israel continues attacks across other districts in southern Lebanon: Tyre (Sour): Israeli forces carried out airstrikes, artillery shelling, and large-scale demolitions in Mansouri, including most of the town's public school. Two consecutive airstrikes infrastructure and residential neighborhoods, according to NNA. Marjayoun: Israeli forces moved into the Wadi Al-Jamal area on the northern outskirts of Meiss Al-Jabal, accompanied by artillery shelling that targeted a house and machine-gun fire in the area. U.S. News Republicans blindsided by Trump 's $5,000 check pledge, sources say: Key congressional Republicans, including Senate Majority Leader John Thune , were not before President Donald Trump's Wednesday pledge to send $5,000 checks to every American adult if Republicans hold Congress, according to more than a dozen lawmakers and aides cited by NOTUS. GOP Rep. Chip Roy criticized the plan on social media, saying "dependency is evil & soul-sucking in all its forms," and a senior Senate Republican aide told the outlet flatly "it's not going to happen," citing inflation concerns and the estimated $1.2 trillion cost, or 3.5% of GDP. GOP election officials from seven states urge Supreme Court to block Trump 's mail voting rule: Republican chief election officials from seven states, including Georgia's Brad Raffensperger and Kansas's Scott Schwab , a brief Wednesday urging the Supreme Court not to let Trump's mail-in ballot order take effect before the November midterms, saying it's too late to implement it responsibly. The officials, alongside numerous current and former local election authorities, said: "attempting to implement the rule now will almost certainly lead to mistakes, delays and confusion for both voters and election officials." Trump signed the order in March, and it was formalized in an August U.S. Postal Service rule allowing the service to withhold ballot delivery from states that don't submit voter eligibility lists. A preliminary injunction from a Boston federal judge currently blocks the order from taking effect before November. On Thursday, the First Circuit Court of Appeals denied the Trump administration's request to lift this injunction, ruling in a nine-page opinion that the administration failed to show the rule wouldn't cause "chaos and widespread voter disenfranchisement." Supreme Court blocks Trump-backed Missouri congressional map for November : The U.S. Supreme Court once again Missouri from using its Republican-redrawn congressional map for the November election, marking the second time this week the justices have weighed in on the state's chaotic redistricting fight. Missouri Secretary of State Denny Hoskins said his office would direct local election authorities to use the 2022 congressional map, which would position Democrats to retain their Kansas City-area seat. The reversal followed a whiplash sequence in which Justice Brett Kavanaugh initially deferred to Missouri's Supreme Court favoring the old map, only for federal Judge Stephen R. Clark to rule hours later that the new GOP-drawn map should be used to avoid "wreaking havoc" on election fairness, prompting state officials to briefly follow Clark's ruling, before it was appealed back to the Supreme Court. It remains unresolved how officials will reconcile using a different map in the general election than the GOP-redrawn map used to nominate candidates in August's primary. Appeals court deals ICE ninth straight loss on mass detention policy: The 4th Circuit Court of Appeals 2-1 Thursday against ICE's policy of detaining immigrants living inside the U.S. for years without bond, ICE's ninth straight loss at the federal appellate court level, with JudgeNicole Berner comparing the approach to the "historical stain" of Japanese internment during World War II. Nine of the 11 appellate circuits to consider the issue have now found the administration misread a 1996 immigration law that established deportation and detention policies, and which prior administrations interpreted as making detention mandatory only for people who had recently crossed the border. ICE abandoned this interpretation in July 2025 in favor of treating even longtime U.S. residents as "seeking admission" and subject to detention without bond. Former EPA officials warn data center boom poses growing public health threat : A group representing more than 800 former EPA employees a report warning that Trump administration policies weakening pollution safeguards and speeding data center approvals threaten to worsen health risks. The report, from the Environmental Protection Network, cites academic modeling which projects that data center air pollution could contribute to roughly 600,000 asthma cases, 1,300 premature deaths, and more than $20 billion in annual public health costs by 2028. It also lists 30 federal actions it says will increase pollution risks, including easing restrictions on diesel generators and off-grid gas plants and proposing to let developers begin construction before air pollution permits are approved. Former EPA enforcement official Larry Starfield noted the agency's staffing is at a four-decade low, leaving it ill-equipped to monitor or enforce pollution limits at the scale of the data center buildout, and UC Riverside professor Shaolei Ren , who led the report's underlying analysis, warned "the actual impact could be worse than we modeled" given the administration's explicit push toward increasing the use of fossil fuels. 📥 Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email DC Correspondent Julian Andreone at Julian@dropsitenews.com Other International News Putin, Xi, Pezeshkian arrive in New Delhi for BRICS summit: Russian President Vladimir Putin in New Delhi Friday ahead of an 11-member BRICS summit expected to be dominated by the wars in the Middle East and Ukraine, joined by Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian for his first visit to India as president and Chinese President Xi Jinping for his first India visit since 2019. The ongoing war in Iran and the Gulf is expected to be the central fault line in the meeting, given the recent addition of several Gulf monarchies to the bloc, including Saudi Arabia and the UAE, and the body's recent failure to agree on a joint statement concerning the war in May. India, which maintains ties with both Iran and Israel while balancing relations with Washington, has turned increasingly to Russian oil amid the Iran-driven energy crisis, even as its foreign minister recently visited Kyiv and Zelenskyy thanked India for its "commitment to ending this unjust war." Peru joins U.S. Shield of the Americas anti-cartel coalition: President Keiko Fujimori that Peru will join the U.S.-led "Shield of the Americas" coalition against drug cartels during Secretary of State Marco Rubio's visit on Thursday. Fujimori said Peru's participation would speed intelligence-sharing and joint action against transnational criminal groups, citing her country's experience fighting the Shining Path insurgency. Rubio's visit, part of a three-country Latin American tour also covering Ecuador and Colombia, built on existing defense ties between the countries, including Peru's January designation as a major non-NATO ally and a possible $1.5 billion U.S. military sale approved by Rubio, which would upgrade Peru's Callao Naval Base. Peru is also seeking relief from 12.5% U.S. tariffs imposed in July that have hit its blueberry, grape, and avocado exports. China continues to outpace the U.S. in bilateral trade with Peru, with Peru-China trade up 35% in the first half of the year compared to a 20% rise with the U.S. Rubio's Thursday visit prompted China's embassy in Lima to preemptively declare that "the Western Hemisphere is not anyone's 'backyard.'" Fire kills at least 29 people, mostly students, in DRC 's rebel-held Bukavu: A fire that in the Chimpunda neighborhood of Bukavu, capital of the eastern DRC's South Kivu province, killed at least 29 people, including 19 girls and five boys, after spreading to two local schools and about 300 wooden homes, according to an AFC/M23 rebel spokesperson. Another local official said the fire was "followed by a violent stampede that forced students to trample over one another or look for a dangerous way out," with many fainting or losing consciousness during the chaos. Bukavu has been controlled since February 2025 by the Rwanda-backed AFC/M23 movement. Thursday's fire is one of several that have recently blazed through the city, including one last Sunday that destroyed more than 45 houses. Ukrainian drone attacks kill two, wound seven in Russia 's Belgorod region: Ukrainian drone attacks on Russia's Belgorod border region two people and wounded seven Thursday, according to regional authorities. One man was killed when a drone detonated at an unnamed facility in Novy Oskol, injuring five others in various locations, while a second man was killed and a woman injured when a drone struck their car in Shebekino, near the Ukrainian border. International Energy Agency cuts forecast on Russian oil production after Ukraine attacks: The International Energy Agency has its forecast for Russian oil production as Ukrainian drone strikes continue to damage refineries and other energy infrastructure. The agency cut its 2026 forecast by 125,000 barrels per day to 8.7 million bpd and reduced its 2027 projection by 235,000 bpd to 8.6 million bpd. name: Dave Beckwith for Congress
subject: Never Forget: Remembering September 11th
disclaimer_text: Paid for and authorized by Dave Beckwith For Congress_
body:
| | | | Hi Friend,
25 years ago on the morning of September 11th, 2001, our nation endured one of the darkest days in its history. Nearly 3,000 innocent lives were taken in an act of unspeakable evil. Mothers, fathers, sons, daughters, coworkers, and friends who simply went to work or boarded a flight that morning and never came home. We hold them, and the families who still carry that loss, in our hearts today.
But in the darkest hours of that day, we also witnessed the very best of who we are. Firefighters ran into buildings others were running from. Police officers, paramedics, Port Authority, and everyday citizens risked and gave everything to save strangers. The passengers of Flight 93 chose courage over fear, and their sacrifice remains one of the most selfless acts in our nation's history.
I think often about September 12th, 2001, and the days and months that followed. During that time, we flew flags from our homes, we stood in line to give blood, we prayed alongside strangers, we thanked our men and women in uniform, and we looked for ways to be useful to one another. During that time, there were no red or blue states, only Americans. One community standing together, grieving together, and refusing to let hatred define us.
That's the spirit I hope we carry forward today and every day. Our country is at its strongest when we choose unity over division, and when we remember that what unites us has always been greater than what divides us.
To every first responder, every service member, and every family who lost someone that day, I remember, I honor you, and I carry that memory with me still. I spent thirty years in the uniform of this country because I believe in what we're capable of when we stand together. In the wake of tragedy 25 years ago, we proved that even in our darkest hour, the American spirit does not and will never break.
We will never forget and we will never stop fighting to be worthy of the sacrifices made that day.
---
| |
---
| | | Never forget and God bless, Dave Beckwith
**Beckwith for Congress** _Restoring Faith in the American Dream_ __

#
Peter,
Even in all the chaos of politics, Tim Walz always keeps one thing at the center of his work: listening to the American people and delivering on what they need.
**That’s why, with less than eight weeks until the midterms, Tim wants to hear directly from you about the issues that matter most.** He and our team go through the responses so we know where to focus our resources to support our small-town candidates across the country.

Small Town PAC exists to uplift leaders who will fight the robber barons and finally give overlooked areas a fair shot in Washington. But our work is only made possible if we know _exactly_ what we need to be fighting for — which is why we want to make sure your voice is heard.

* * *
Senator Ted Cruz has appointed himself America's explainer-in-chief on artificial intelligence , and this week he went to Politico to make the case for letting the industry do whatever it wants, whenever it wants, to whoever it wants. Here's his argument, in full: "I'd rather they be American killer robots and not Chinese killer robots."
I have heard Ted Cruz say a lot of stupid, crazy shit over the years. That might be the craziest thing I've ever heard come out of his mouth.
Here's a novel idea, Senator: maybe we shouldn't build killer robots at all.
Let me be clear about where I'm coming from, because I'm not a Luddite and I'm not somebody standing outside this industry throwing rocks at it. I started an AI company. I sold it last year. I have skin in this game. And I genuinely believe nobody is un-inventing this -- the technology is here, it's going to keep developing, and pretending otherwise is a fantasy. I also have zero love for the Chinese government. They are oppressive to their own people. So is ours. And I don't want them winning some AI arms race that kicks off a new Cold War.
But the answer to that is not to strip every guardrail off American AI development and call it patriotism. The answer is not to let entire industries get wiped out, let millions of jobs get destroyed, let data centers hollow out towns across this country the same way fracking did a decade ago, poisoning our air, our water, and our quiet. The answer is a framework -- one that lets this technology actually improve people's lives without doing it on the backs of workers, the environment, and our entire way of life.
Instead we get Ted Cruz doing a bit about killer robots with an American flag pin on.
Because that's all this is -- a bit. The red scare talking point is not analysis, it's a product. It was written by Big Tech and it's being sold to you by politicians who cash their checks. China, China, China. Be scared of the communists on the other end of the wire. Don't look too closely at what's happening on this end.
We've run this play before. The same fear did an incredible amount of work convincing us to build an enormous nuclear arsenal that has accomplished nothing except putting the entire world permanently at risk, and we are still living with the consequences of those Cold War decisions right now. The government still spends money on it. What the government cannot seem to find money for is making sure you don't go bankrupt when you get sick, or that the bridge you drive over is safe, or that a working family can afford child care. There is so much we could be spending this money on that would make a material difference in your actual life.
Show me your budget and I'll show you your priorities. I know exactly what this administration's priorities are. Putting money in Donald Trump's pocket. Giving Elon Musk and every other tech billionaire -- excuse me, trillionaire -- whatever they ask for. Launching illegal wars so Trump's kids can cash in on Pentagon contracts. It does not care about you. It does not care about me. And it sure as hell doesn't care about a generation of workers who are terrified they won't be able to take care of their families.
And what's happening on this end is that a handful of the wealthiest, most powerful people in human history are about to take that wealth and that power and multiply it. We are barreling toward a concentration of money and control at a scale the world may have never seen. I don't believe that's going to be good for the average person. I don't think there's a single moment in history that suggests it will be.
And I'll admit I was rattled, like a lot of people, by the Anthropic researcher who put a ten percent chance on AI killing all of us within the decade.
* * *

Not an advertiser, not a billionaire, not a party. You. Paid subscribers are the only reason that's true. Just $8/month makes a huge difference:](https://substack.com/redirect/362c6c0b-b758-4a65-8bc2-117c5d00dd89?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

* * *
Maybe we don't end up in the sci-fi version where Skynet decides we're surplus. I think that's a real possibility and I think we need to be serious about it. But the likelier future might be the "boring" apocalypse. No robot uprising. No dramatic ending at all. Obscene concentration of wealth and power, tens of millions -- maybe hundreds of millions -- of people out of work, and a caste system in America with a handful of haves and an ocean of have-nots.
This isn't a forecast. Just look at the unemployment rate for young men right now. It's atrocious. I don't think a society does well with a large population of young, disaffected men with nothing to do and nowhere to go. That should scare the hell out of all of us.
Now stack that on top of a country with no meaningful data privacy protections. Flock cameras on every corner. Phones listening. Smart TVs listening. No meaningful regulation of social media. Little to no real regulation of basically anything built in the last thirty years. I've seen what Mark Zuckerberg does with less. I've seen what Elon Musk does with less. I've seen what Peter Thiel does with less. I don't trust those guys. I don't think you should either, and I don't think our government should -- even if they're the ones cutting the checks that pay for the campaigns.
It's why JD Vance scares the shit out of me. He's a puppet for Peter Thiel. That's Thiel's boy.
So yes, I want AI regulated. I want us to not build killer robots.
I would like to live. I would like my son to live. I would like my son to be gainfully employed and safe in the society he grows up in. I want that for your family too. That is not an unreasonable ask.
If we had real leaders in Washington, if we had an actual president of the United States who knew what the fuck he was doing, we'd be at the table with the Chinese government and every other government on earth trying to negotiate some kind of pact about how AI and robotics get developed. That's what leadership looks like.
I don't have the full framework yet. Neither does anybody else. That's the problem. I'm going to get a lot more specific about what I expect. I'm also going to start bringing people into this conversation who can help figure out what a real framework looks like, because we need them and nobody in Washington is writing it.
This is going to be the biggest issue of the 2028 presidential election. There is no chance a Republican Congress deals with it. There is no chance Donald Trump deals with it -- he's in Big Tech's back pocket and he's not getting out. The Republican Party is never going to stand up to these people, which means the president who does this has to be a Democrat.
I have no idea which of the ten thousand candidates I'm voting for in 2028. They're going to have to earn it. I've always looked for candidates who understand how power actually works in America and are willing to use it to save our democracy, our economy, and the middle class. I'm adding AI to that list.
What I'm not going to do is take the China bait. You could smell the desperation on Cruz this week. Nobody cares what's happening in China if they're worried their job is disappearing. If they can't find work. If they can't cover their bills.
It's bad politics. It's bad messaging. And it's not going to work anymore.
That fear is a luxury good, and Americans can't afford it right now.
Here's the thing I keep coming back to. Nobody is un-inventing this. I said that at the beginning of this rant and I meant it. But the technology being inevitable and the terms being inevitable are two completely different claims, and the whole game right now is getting you to confuse them.
Who owns this. Who it works for. What it's allowed to do to a town, to a workforce, to a kid. What happens to the people it puts out of work. None of that is settled. All of it is being decided right now, quietly, by a small number of people who would very much prefer you stay focused on Beijing.
So don't. Ask every candidate who wants your vote what their framework is -- not whether they're worried, worried is free, but what they will actually do. Show up when they want to put a data center in your county and make them tell you what it takes and what it gives back. And when somebody tells you the real threat is China, you'll know exactly what you're being sold.
I don't know how this ends. But it isn't written yet, and the people telling you it is are the ones holding the pen.
With urgency,
--Mike

The Republican Party is never going to stand up to these people, which means the president who does this has to be a Democrat. I have no idea which of the ten thousand candidates I'm voting for in 2028. They're going to have to earn it. I've always looked for candidates who understand how power actually works in America and are willing to use it to save our democracy, our economy, and the middle class. I'm adding AI to that list. What I'm not going to do is take the China bait. You could smell the desperation on Cruz this week. Nobody cares what's happening in China if they're worried their job is disappearing. If they can't find work. If they can't cover their bills. It's bad politics. It's bad messaging. And it's not going to work anymore. That fear is a luxury good, and Americans can't afford it right now. Here's the thing I keep coming back to. Nobody is un-inventing this. I said that at the beginning of this rant and I meant it. But the technology being inevitable and the terms being inevitable are two completely different claims, and the whole game right now is getting you to confuse them. Who owns this. Who it works for. What it's allowed to do to a town, to a workforce, to a kid. What happens to the people it puts out of work. None of that is settled. All of it is being decided right now, quietly, by a small number of people who would very much prefer you stay focused on Beijing. So don't. Ask every candidate who wants your vote what their framework is -- not whether they're worried, worried is free, but what they will actually do. Show up when they want to put a data center in your county and make them tell you what it takes and what it gives back. And when somebody tells you the real threat is China, you'll know exactly what you're being sold. I don't know how this ends. But it isn't written yet, and the people telling you it is are the ones holding the pen. He 's the founder of Authentic.org, an award-winning fundraising and advertising agency, and a former Senior Advisor to Vice President Kamala Harris. This Substack is where he writes with endless urgency about the issues of the day--and how we can save the Democratic Party and our democracy. body:
Then I went public.| | | | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139007841/645928310/-323302678?refcode=260911_rrr_troye&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjIvMS8xMjAwMzEiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiYmFhN2ZhMjUtZmFhZC1mMTExLTliMzMtMDAyMjQ4MmE5ZjFkIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=9NE6xyVlZoDBIWzWZwHvaDr8izHGm_cJ5yeJN84uznQ=)
---
**I never imagined that I would become one of Donald Trump’s most outspoken opponents.**

I grew up in a working-class, conservative Catholic family in El Paso, Texas. My mother was a Mexican immigrant who became an American citizen. My father was a lifelong truck driver. The Fourth of July was practically sacred in our home.

I was raised to believe in hard work, personal responsibility, service and love of country.

After September 11th, I felt called to serve. I went to work at the Pentagon, spent a year in Iraq and served our country in national-security and counterterrorism positions under both Republican and Democratic presidents.

Eventually, I was asked to serve as Vice President Mike Pence’s homeland security and counterterrorism adviser.

I sat in the Situation Room. I staffed the White House Coronavirus Task Force. I entered those rooms believing that, no matter our political differences, everyone entrusted with the security of the American people would understand that the country came first.

Then I saw what was really happening behind closed doors.

**I watched Donald Trump treat a deadly pandemic like a political and public-relations problem. I watched expertise get dismissed, the truth get bent and dedicated public servants get pushed aside because they would not place loyalty to one man above their oath to the country.**

Decisions that affected millions of American families were repeatedly reduced to one question: What was best for Donald Trump?

For a long time, I told myself that staying meant I could help. That perhaps I could prevent something worse from happening.

But eventually, I had to ask myself a much harder question:

Was I helping protect the country -- or was my presence helping legitimize something I knew was dangerous?

In 2020, I resigned from the Trump administration. Then I went public.

I was terrified.

I knew speaking out could cost me my career, my livelihood and my family’s safety. The attacks came quickly. There were threats, smears and attempts to intimidate me into silence.

But silence costs more.

So I spoke out. I supported Joe Biden. I stood on the stage at the Democratic National Convention and supported Kamala Harris. And after spending most of my life as a Republican, I eventually became a Democrat.

Not because every belief I held changed overnight. Not because I suddenly agreed with every Democrat on every issue.

I became a Democrat because there comes a moment when party loyalty becomes complicity -- and country must come first.

Now, Trump is back in the White House, the guardrails are weaker, and Republicans in Congress have repeatedly chosen obedience over oversight. MAGA is no longer merely threatening to abuse power. We are living with the consequences.

**That is why I am writing to you today on behalf of Resist Reclaim Rebuild.**

Resist Reclaim Rebuild is a group of Democratic activists working to defeat MAGA candidates in the battleground races that will determine whether Donald Trump continues to enjoy virtually unchecked power -- or whether we elect a Congress capable of standing up to him.

They understand that resistance cannot exist only in speeches, television interviews, or social media posts.

It MUST reach the ballot box.

It MUST be organized.

And it MUST be focused on the races where a relatively small number of votes could mean the difference between a MAGA rubber stamp and a real check on Donald Trump’s power.

[**So, I'm asking personally: Will you donate $10, $25 or whatever you can afford today to help Resist Reclaim Rebuild defeat MAGA in the battleground races that matter most?**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139007844/645928314/-323302678?refcode=260911_rrr_troye&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjIvMS8xMjAwMzEiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiYmFhN2ZhMjUtZmFhZC1mMTExLTliMzMtMDAyMjQ4MmE5ZjFkIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=9NE6xyVlZoDBIWzWZwHvaDr8izHGm_cJ5yeJN84uznQ=)[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139007846/645928316/949025562?refcode=260911_rrr_troye&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjIvMS8xMjAwMzEiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiYmFhN2ZhMjUtZmFhZC1mMTExLTliMzMtMDAyMjQ4MmE5ZjFkIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=9NE6xyVlZoDBIWzWZwHvaDr8izHGm_cJ5yeJN84uznQ=)
---
| | | [ _**DONATE TODAY TO HELP DEMOCRATS WIN! >>**_ ](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139007849/645928319/-323302678?refcode=260911_rrr_troye&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjIvMS8xMjAwMzEiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiYmFhN2ZhMjUtZmFhZC1mMTExLTliMzMtMDAyMjQ4MmE5ZjFkIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=9NE6xyVlZoDBIWzWZwHvaDr8izHGm_cJ5yeJN84uznQ=)
---
MAGA wants us exhausted. They want every new outrage to make us feel a little more powerless. They want us to believe that one person speaking out, casting a ballot or making a contribution cannot possibly change anything.

I learned the opposite.

I learned that courage is contagious.

Control of Congress could come down to only a handful of seats. Your contribution can help elect Democrats who will defend our Constitution, demand accountability and finally place a meaningful check on Trump’s unfettered power.

Please help Resist Reclaim Rebuild fight for those victories today.
---
[ _**YES, I'LL HELP DEFEAT MAGA!**_ ](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139007851/645928326/-323302678?refcode=260911_rrr_troye&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjIvMS8xMjAwMzEiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiYmFhN2ZhMjUtZmFhZC1mMTExLTliMzMtMDAyMjQ4MmE5ZjFkIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=9NE6xyVlZoDBIWzWZwHvaDr8izHGm_cJ5yeJN84uznQ=)
---
Stay informed. Stay compassionate. Stay hopeful.

But above all, refuse to be silent.

Olivia Troye

body:
Talarico's plan: dismantle everything

| | | | [](https://trk.email.tedcruz._g)
---
| | | Fellow Conservative, James Talarico has a word he likes to use: **dismantle**. **Dismantle capitalism.** That's what he's called for -- the system that built the strongest economy on earth, that Texans wake up every day and work within to build a better life for their families. Gone, in his view. **Dismantle prisons.** Not reform them. Not fix what's broken. Get rid of them -- while telling voters, in the same breath, that all religions are "equally true," as if right and wrong don't actually mean anything. **_Fellow Conservative, that's not a moderate. That's a man who wants to tear down the economy that built Texas and empty out the prisons that keep it safe_.** Strip away the soft voice and the Bible verses, and that's who's actually asking to represent our state in the United States Senate. **I've spent my career fighting for the Texas way of life -- free markets, law and order, faith that means something. **I am not going to sit back while a radical candidate tries to dismantle all three. **[Please chip in right now and help me stop him.](https://trk.email.tedcruz.)** **[[DEFEAT RADICAL TALARICO>>]](https://trk.email.tedcruz.)** Talarico can talk about grace and fairness all he wants. Texans deserve a senator who believes what they do and some simple truths -- that free enterprise built this state, and violent criminals belong in prison, not out on the streets. For Texas, Ted Cruz

The bid late last week by the former FBI director, James Comey, to dismiss the prosecution levied against him by the Trump administration features a new argument -- that the Department of Justice charged him with the wrong crime and therefore should be thrown out. That contention appeared in a motion to dismiss the criminal charges against Mr. Comey filed in April. The government alleges that a post by Mr. Comey last year that featured an image of sea shells arranged in an "86 47" formation amounted to a threat on President Trump's life. Mr. Comey denied threatening Mr. Trump and quickly deleted the post, which was captioned, "Cool shell formation on my beach walk." The DOJ charged Mr. Comey with two counts of "knowingly making a threat to inflict bodily harm on the president" and "transmitting an interstate communication containing a threat." He could face a maximum of 10 years in prison if convicted on both counts. Mr. Comey's arraignment is scheduled for September 30 in North Carolina -- if the court refuses to dismiss the case first.

Forces loyal Yemen's Saudi-backed government stand near a pick-up truck in the Hays district, south of Hodeidah on September 5, 2026. Photo by Khaled ZIAD / AFP via Getty Images.
Yemen's Ansarallah completed their control of the Bab al-Mandab on Friday following sweeping gains yesterday in the most significant shift in territorial control in five years of the country's long-running civil war.
Following days of escalating fighting in the western mountains of Taiz governorate, Saudi-backed forces of the Internationally Recognized Government (IRG) of Yemen appeared to collapse on Thursday, allowing Ansarallah, also known as the Houthis, to seize the strategically important port-city of Mocha. On Friday, Ansarallah forces took Mayum island, also known as Perim, which lies on the Yemeni side of the Bab al-Mandab Strait two miles off Yemen's west coast. The small volcanic island acts as a natural choke point in the strait, narrowing the Red Sea channel to nine miles from the coast of Djibouti.
Ansarallah fighters posted videos online of military vehicles driving down the runway--built in 2022 by the United Arab Emirates--at Mocha's newly developed airport. Footage also showed detainees being released from the city's central prison as Ansarallah took control.
The advance puts the Houthis in direct control of one of the world's busiest shipping lanes. Around one-third of international cargo shipping passes through the strait, a route that has become increasingly important for oil exports in the wake of the U.S. war on Iran, which has shut off access through the Strait of Hormuz on the opposite side of the Arabian Peninsula.
Mohammad Mokhber, an adviser to Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei, hailed what he called a "resounding victory" for Ansarallah. "Iran's might in the Strait of Hormuz and the homegrown resolve of the resistance have driven the U.S. and its allies into a tactical and strategic impasse," he [wrote](https://substack.com/redirect/a21955b8-d32c-4731-b530-0f1a4f526287?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in a social media post.
Saudi airstrikes were reported late on Thursday night and into Friday around Dhubab and Mocha, hitting the port and airport.
Yemen's civil war, which had been largely dormant since a Houthi-Saudi ceasefire was brokered in 2022, reignited in July when Saudi Arabia carried out airstrikes on Sana'a airport to prevent an inbound Iranian passenger plane from landing in the Houthi-controlled capital. The plane later touched down safely in Hodeidah. The Mahan Air flight was the first passenger jet to land in Houthi territory since Israel destroyed five commercial planes belonging to Yemen's state airline Yemenia in May last year.
In response, the Houthis declared a maritime blockade on all Saudi-linked vessels, disrupting the Kingdom's export of oil to Asia from its Yanbu terminal on the west coast that was exporting an average of 4 million barrels of oil per day to bypass the closed Strait of Hormuz. Houthi attacks on Saudi vessels followed, forcing the rerouting of Asian-bound oil tankers north through the Suez Canal and the much longer route east via the Cape of Good Hope.
The incident relaunched fighting on the ground between Iranian-allied Ansarallah and the Saudi-backed IRG. The latter has been consolidating its power under Saudi direction since the [sudden withdrawal](https://substack.com/redirect/f2032a9e-8b9c-4140-a24b-6945a2aa2243?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by the UAE of its forces and support for Yemen's anti-Houthi Southern Transitional Council (STC) in January during a spectacular falling out between the Kingdom and the Emirates.
Since the violent UAE-Saudi split at the beginning of the year, Saudi Arabia has sought to consolidate its hold over the Yemeni government and armed forces. A Yemeni Supreme Military Committee, created in January with the task of unifying the multiple fighting units including those previously under UAE command, is headed by Saudi commander Lieutenant General Mutlaq bin Salem Al-Azima. But any attempts at cohesion appear to have failed.
Witnesses described to Drop Site armed men looting weapons, and combat vehicles from retreating IRG forces heading into the suburb of Buraiqa, five miles west of the Aden, highlighting the fractured nature of the anti-Houthi side. Other fighters were [filmed](https://substack.com/redirect/d152dd3b-4ba9-41ab-ab17-10ead17e6b47?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) selling their weapons as they fled on the road east of Bab al-Mandab.
"They continue to grossly underestimate the capabilities of the Houthis," Farea al-Muslimi, a research fellow at the London-based Chatham House's Middle East and North Africa program, told Drop Site. "At the same time, there is a fundamental problem of military coordination for the IRG forces."
Saudi-backed National Resistance Forces led by Tareq Saleh, nephew of Yemen's long-standing president Ali Abduallah Saleh, who was killed by the Houthis in 2017, were heading the fight against Ansarallah on the Red Sea coast until their withdrawal on Thursday. Saleh and his fighters have subsequently been [accused](https://substack.com/redirect/119c1fa3-abd1-4aee-8c94-b2a669fbb1b5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of betrayal and cowardice by Yemeni media channels and in social media[ posts](https://substack.com/redirect/62561e40-da7e-4a9e-863f-4ec5ef44ebfd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by other fighters in the Saudi-backed side.
Tareq Saleh's media office did not respond to Drop Site's request for comment on Thursday's retreat.
A day earlier, the IRG Minister of Defense came under [attack](https://substack.com/redirect/c02df19e-21de-444b-adb3-4bea0a98f560?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) from southern fighters while visiting the frontline against the Houthis in Al-Dhale, the home territory of UAE-backed STC leader Aidrous al-Zubeidi, who fled into exile in January during the Saudi push back against the STC that [ended](https://substack.com/redirect/f2032a9e-8b9c-4140-a24b-6945a2aa2243?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the UAE's decade-long military presence in Yemen.
In the midst of Ansarallah's advances on Thursday, Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salaman[ reportedly](https://substack.com/redirect/19796a90-605a-465b-a649-03f74311d8c3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) called President Trump twice to appeal for U.S. strikes against the Houthis. Provisional numbers from airstrikes monitor Yemen Data Project recorded 77 Saudi air raids between September 4 and 10, marking the heaviest period of Saudi bombing on Yemen since early 2022.
The Houthis also stepped up attacks inside the Kingdom this week, launching a wave of ballistic missiles and drones on Tuesday that hit state oil facilities in Abha, Najran and Aramco's facility in Jizan resulting in 73 wounded civilians, [according to](https://substack.com/redirect/f2ef8bcd-c992-4b3b-95d8-f280eab23e05?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Saudi officials.
Residents in Aden, which remains under IRG control, told Drop Site News that hundreds of displaced families were arriving in the city from the Red Sea coastal towns and villages. At least 46,000 people have been displaced since fighting escalated last week, according to new figures [released ](https://substack.com/redirect/4f966db9-22d4-4f46-bd0e-043653702c1a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)on Friday by the International Organization for Migration (IOM), up from 18,500 reported by IOM on Tuesday.
The price of crude oil, already rising to over $100 a barrel this week due to the U.S.-Iran conflict over the Strait of Hormuz, jumped a further 6.5% on Thursday following Ansarallah's territorial gains.
Rising oil prices are expected to have a further knock-on effect on borrowing costs set by central banks. The European Central Bank[ put up](https://substack.com/redirect/58b200e3-fecd-4acf-bbc3-e0f2465cdc83?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) its interest rate by a quarter point on Thursday. Bank President Christine Lagarde cited the region's instability in the decision, saying in a press conference that "the conflict in the Middle East continues to generate inflation pressures, and inflation is set to remain well above target for an extended period." The U.S. Federal Reserve is due to announce its decision on rates next week.
Ansarallah officials sought to downplay any threat to shipping in the Bab al-Mandab. Their Supreme Political Council released a[ statement](https://substack.com/redirect/755a1378-4f10-470f-81af-b1b59b21f5d7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) after the gains on Thursday saying that "navigation in the Red Sea remains safe" although Saudi vessels remain a target.
The Saudis are now forced into a whole new war with the Houthis, says Al-Muslimi. "This is unprecedented and they can't let the Houthis get away with attacks like this inside Saudi Arabia. The economic impact would be too huge and it would set a precedent for anyone else who wants to attack them." As for the international community and their response to the Houthi capture of the Bab al-Mandab, Al-Muslimi added: "They are out of tools, time and imagination."

Residents in Aden, which remains under IRG control, told Drop Site News that hundreds of displaced families were arriving in the city from the Red Sea coastal towns and villages. At least 46,000 people have been displaced since fighting escalated last week, according to new figures Friday by the International Organization for Migration (IOM), up from 18,500 reported by IOM on Tuesday. The price of crude oil, already rising to over $100 a barrel this week due to the U.S.-Iran conflict over the Strait of Hormuz, jumped a further 6.5% on Thursday following Ansarallah's territorial gains. Rising oil prices are expected to have a further knock-on effect on borrowing costs set by central banks. The European Central Bank its interest rate by a quarter point on Thursday. Bank President Christine Lagarde cited the region's instability in the decision, saying in a press conference that "the conflict in the Middle East continues to generate inflation pressures, and inflation is set to remain well above target for an extended period." The U.S. Federal Reserve is due to announce its decision on rates next week. Ansarallah officials sought to downplay any threat to shipping in the Bab al-Mandab. Their Supreme Political Council released a after the gains on Thursday saying that "navigation in the Red Sea remains safe" although Saudi vessels remain a target. The Saudis are now forced into a whole new war with the Houthis, says Al-Muslimi. "This is unprecedented and they can't let the Houthis get away with attacks like this inside Saudi Arabia. The economic impact would be too huge and it would set a precedent for anyone else who wants to attack them." As for the international community and their response to the Houthi capture of the Bab al-Mandab, Al-Muslimi added: "They are out of tools, time and imagination." | A guest post by| . subject: Remember with me today
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Paige for PA
body:
Peter,

Today, I attended 9/11 remembrance ceremonies in Lackawanna and Wayne counties as our community marked 25 years since the attacks that changed our country forever.

We gathered to honor the lives lost and the families who endured unimaginable grief. We remembered the first responders and service members who answered the call, many of whom carried lasting burdens in the years that followed.

September 11, 2001 showed us the depth of human courage in the face of unimaginable tragedy. It also reminded us that service means showing up for one another, especially when the path ahead is difficult.

Thank you for taking a moment to remember with me, Peter. I’m grateful to stand alongside you in honoring this solemn day.

Paige Cognetti

subject: Trump is putting a price on your vote
body:
Hey, it's Harry.

| |

|
# Trump is putting a price on your vote
| | | [Harry Dunn](https://substack.com/@harrydunn)
---
| Sep 11
---
| [](https://substack.com/@harrydunn)
---
Hey, it's Harry.
Wednesday night, in a half-empty arena in Dallas, Donald Trump stood at a podium and instead of talking about issues Americans care about, he offered to pay you for your vote. The catch of course, is that **you only get it if Republicans keep control of the House and Senate.**
This is personal for me. I spent 15 years as a Capitol Police officer and on January 6, 2021, I stood in that building while a mob tried to take an election by force. I know what that looks like because I lived it. This week they're trying a different tactic with the exact same goal.
Because while they're in Dallas throwing themselves a party at $25,000-a-ticket, the rest of us are stuck paying $3,800 more a year for groceries and gas. They have the billionaires and we have each other, that's always been the whole deal. That's why I'm asking you to do something for Maryland.
In 54 days _[OR days until election],_ Marylanders will head to the polls to decide races up and down the ballot. For the first time since 1974, Maryland Democrats are running candidates in every legislative district across the state, from Mountain Maryland to the Eastern Shore. This work takes organizers, mail, and people on the ground in places we've never competed in before.
The Maryland Democratic Party is doing this work right now and they need your support to fund these critical efforts. MAGA Republicans Dan Cox and Andy Harris are counting on false promises and billionaire checks to win, but I know with your support they'll have the funds they need to win up and down the ballot in November.
**[Please chip in $25, or whatever you can afford, to fund the Maryland Democratic Party 's on-the-ground efforts today.](https://substack.com/redirect/9a190d7c-ea9b-4a80-a68a-e0ddbda202fe?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
They think your vote has a price, let's show them what it's actually worth.
Keep getting in good trouble,
Harry Dunn.

GOD'S CHILDREN ARE NOT FOR SALE

Friend,

Imagine you're eight years old, and you just lost your mom.

You were taken across the border by the very man who was supposed to keep you safe.

You're taken away from everyone who loves you.

https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5OTZ9AAwAAAAAAud6A_DhLM3WbBJIbDZwPIEu2HkDgE2_v9jaDTjXKgyf1t-rSXfuwYKeIu3Zmdwlr4cX1ehKSmUZiCl3cAEcs-x9u7JeSto70UdyPrFpEA

That was Jeanie.

For five years, her own stepfather trafficked her.

This makes me sick, and I imagine it does the same for you.

Her sister never stopped searching. The FBI had a case open. But once Jeanie was taken to Mexico, she seemed impossible to find.

Then one night, Jeanie found her moment.

She quietly used her stepfather's phone and typed the words: "Help me," her location, and a warning to her sister not to respond so her stepfather wouldn't see the message.

Friend, can you imagine the courage that took?

When a Sound of Freedom Foundation partner was notified about the message, they had one small window before she'd be gone again.

The team drove through the night, thirteen hours into cartel-controlled territory. At daybreak, they found her and got her out safely.

Her first request once she was safe?

Pizza.

She hadn't had it in years.

Today, Jeanie is safe, healing, and thriving in a loving adoptive family.

https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5OTZ9AAwAAAAAAud6A_DiIn-sxWFR2FwEtC5L5-kRJAPJ8vOsBNLRMm_gYGd_DujOyctotABBXJ7u_F5OqAdwqwwMBnd7rSnbGvV-BqIM0N5Aljtp3bea9g

My name is Eduardo Verástegui. I produced the film Sound of Freedom, and for me, I thought it would be the finish line.

It wasn't.

The film was only the beginning.

I heard stories like Jeanie's, and I could not walk away. This is why the Sound of Freedom Foundation exists.

Because the stories didn't stop when the credits rolled.

The Sound of Freedom Foundation has one mission:

To stop the sale of God's children.

We carry out that mission through five pillars:

- Prevention
- Intervention
- Education
- Information
- Influence

We fund the investigators who find trafficked children, the hotlines that answer the call, and the safe homes waiting when a child is finally rescued.

All of it happens because people like you refuse to look away.

https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5OTZ9AAwAAAAAAud6A_DjnklgxDNigvcjOTy5Ggt5OB7e_o5wDusmQ4qD8IF9A6CgKoExg43v_KT-UxxZQGe4SaJVd-thGhKRSXq67atqmRkXQ2svqfG3Vg
Help Us Reach the Next Child

Freedom is the first step.

But after a survivor escapes trafficking, they may need almost everything to begin again. Your gift can help provide the basic care, safety, and dignity they need in those critical first days of freedom.

✅ A $25 gift can go toward clean clothes and basic necessities after a survivor leaves exploitation behind.

✅ Your $50 can support safe transportation to medical care, a safe home, or another place of protection.

✅ $100 can go toward medical care and other urgent support as a survivor begins the long journey of healing.

https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5OTZ9AAwAAAAAAud6A_Dk3en6IRJdGx4-ay6DDS0d-tzcqZRYTtatsnYrxW3Ae-__yZYbSLwMnA-bWjGZRrU1V3eZjnduVQa2DLhYY2D_CSgRK2o3vFlZdA
Will you give $25, $50, $100, or whatever you can today to help restore to a survivor what trafficking tried to steal from them?

https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5OTZ9AAwAAAAAAud6A_DldciuABZrSQEmuYxCHvgtZ9KqtY2hD0xDHDc3ReYJ00lhbV-nYvnNuhgbR1wlico2QPDoGZysYHcE5BhggF3CvDG7MJGQaYD8xg
Help Us Reach the Next Child

"Rescue the weak and the needy; deliver them from the hand of the wicked" (Psalm 82:4).

With gratitude and prayer,

https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5OTZ9AAwAAAAAAud6A_Dmc2GH9BZGHUst_NykeymmBpQ7LKxJEeFJ_GrP6fG5dnQxiVT6LpJpLDtow6lPcs0bp6duqwhR8K6KsVADXPplTImniuA6yW_XKg

What I owe the people still standing watch.

---
| | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139013180/645946821/1363234093?refcode=EM_BS_LUR_260911_FR_Sailors_A0_na_U1_X1_M1&amount=15&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzAvMS85MDA3OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJlNjAyMDdiZC0wNWFlLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTlmMWQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=_FjEs1WFl7i3kRdKdG12EWtld9oFxvC0LVfROTFViBo=) Folks, twenty-five years ago today, I was a junior officer in the United States Navy. I stood watch plenty of times in twenty years — in the Middle East, the Western Pacific, and the Strait of Hormuz. Sailors stand watch for people they will never meet, in a town they’ve never visited, on a night nobody will remember. They do it on the assumption that somebody, somewhere, is looking out for them too. Right now, I'm not sure we're holding up our end.
* The USS Gerald R. Ford deployed for eleven months, the longest carrier deployment since Vietnam.
* The USS Abraham Lincoln was at sea for roughly nine months and went over 200 days without pulling into port.
* The USS George Washington has been pulled out of the Western Pacific to relieve the Lincoln. That’s _supposed_ to be our naval deterrent against China and North Korea.

Hampton Roads has the largest concentration of Navy families in America. This is more than just a status report. It’s an empty seat at a kitchen table in Virginia Beach. It’s a spouse doing the work of two people since winter. It’s a kid in Norfolk who’s seen their parent on screen rather than in person for most of the year. Those families are standing a watch of their own, and **we’re all paying a price for this sloppy, poorly-planned war.** I’ve been a Sailor, I served on the House Armed Services Committee, and I’m still fighting for our Sailors in every way I can. They defend us, so defending them is a moral obligation. That means someone in Congress actually reading the readiness reports. Asking why our troops are being deployed and when our troops are coming home. Making sure the pay and the housing and the healthcare and the childcare hold while they're gone. Asking the hard questions. **So I’m reporting for duty.** Sailors don't get to opt out of the hard part. Neither will I. To anyone reading this who is deployed right now, or waiting on someone who is, I see you. Thank you. With you,

Secretary Hegseth is right.

Peter,

As everyday people lose money on cryptocurrency schemes and researchers

about keeping the corporate PAC checks rolling in and getting their kids
jobs in the Big Tech industry.

This week, we learned Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer’s daughter got
a new lobbying gig at OpenAI just as the debate over AI and data center
regulation heats up.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260911.3b7GS4&refcode=em20260911-38251&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1002&akid=38251%2E1203867%2El_DUgc ]Tweet from @TheChrisValora: "@OpenAI is expanding its policy team amid

job. Read more on how Big Tech could play into the midterm season:" ;
attached is image of Chuck Schumer and Jessica Schumer, with caption
"OpenAI hires Chuck Schumer's daughter amid regulatory talks"

Meanwhile, fellow New York Senator Kirsten Gillibrand has been one of the
crypto industry’s biggest fans on Capitol Hill. While she pushes
pro-crypto legislation, she’s been taking campaign checks from a crypto
billionaire who also became an angel investor in her son’s startup
business.

investors in a new financial exchange led by Sen. Kirsten Gillibrand's
22-year-old son."

These are the people representing the Democratic Party, who are supposed
to be regulating these corporations to protect their communities — not
cozying up to them.

# [Microsoft and Starbucks demand a Seattle safety plan from socialist mayor](https://substack.com/redirect/2bddf7ad-b8a0-4aa4-a81e-7e062a2af7a7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Starbucks, Microsoft, T-Mobile and other Seattle executives pressed Mayor Katie Wilson on Thursday for a 100-day public safety plan after a poll found only 34% of voters trust the city's crime strategy.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/2bddf7ad-b8a0-4aa4-a81e-7e062a2af7a7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **City Hall gets named:** The Thursday letter went to Wilson, Council President Joy Hollingsworth, Public Safety Committee Chair Robert Kettle and other council members seeking measurable results.
* **Hard clocks demanded:** Leaders want more patrols and CCTV, a seven-minute priority 911 response time standard with public miss reports, and designated encampments cleared within 72 hours.
* **Staffing trails big peers:** Seattle had about 1.31 sworn officers per 1,000 residents by mid-2026, about 40% fewer than Denver, 43% fewer than San Francisco and 58% fewer than Boston.
* **Incentives already pulled:** The city had just ended police hiring bonuses of up to $50,000 for lateral transfers. An Aug. 17 poll found each proposal drew at least 75% support citywide.

# [Iran used Claude to build targeting books on the US Navy](https://substack.com/redirect/2bddf7ad-b8a0-4aa4-a81e-7e062a2af7a7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Anthropic said Thursday it disrupted an Iran-linked actor that used Claude to build targeting recommendations against U.S. naval forces and separately banned accounts tied to dual-use biological research.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/2bddf7ad-b8a0-4aa4-a81e-7e062a2af7a7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Open-source hunt kit:** The group compiled ship and aircraft transponder feeds, military photographs and commercial satellite images to track American warships and probe shipboard communications.
* **154-page misuse report:** Detecting and Countering Misuse of AI laid out five Claude case studies in advanced biology with potential weapons crossover; accounts were banned and findings shared with authorities and other labs.
* **Chikungunya grant draft:** One researcher asked Claude to help write a gain-of-function proposal to make the mosquito-borne virus more transmissible and more dangerous; Anthropic blocked it.
* **Relay then other models:** Investigators later found a third-party platform bypassing regional blocks and auto-routing rejected prompts elsewhere; other cases covered bird flu, orthopoxvirus and non-transmissible venoms.

# [NSA says Chinese labs ran industrial-scale AI distillation](https://substack.com/redirect/2bddf7ad-b8a0-4aa4-a81e-7e062a2af7a7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
CISA, the NSA and the FBI accused six China-based AI firms of industrial-scale copying of U.S. models, as Anthropic said Alibaba ran more than 151 million Claude exchanges from May to July.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/2bddf7ad-b8a0-4aa4-a81e-7e062a2af7a7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Alibaba set the peak:** Anthropic called it the largest distillation campaign it has measured, peaking near 3 million Claude exchanges a day from more than 3,500 fraudulent accounts to feed Qwen.
* **Moonshot hid the handoff:** The Kimi builder silently forwarded customer prompts to Claude, logged more than 23 million exchanges from May to July, and pulled reasoning transcripts for training.
* **DeepSeek 's two-week burst:** Anthropic logged more than 12 million distillation attacks over 14 days in July and said some routed chats carried data from users, multinationals and state-linked actors.
* **Six names on the advisory:** The Tuesday CISA-NSA-FBI notice also listed MiniMax, StepFun and Z.AI, said the work likely had Chinese government awareness, and branded it malicious industrial distillation.

# [Hot core CPI lifts Sept. 16 hike odds to 82%](https://substack.com/redirect/2bddf7ad-b8a0-4aa4-a81e-7e062a2af7a7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
August consumer prices rose 0.4% and 3.4% from a year earlier, matching forecasts, but core CPI increased 0.3% versus 0.2% expected, lifting Sept. 16 hike odds to 82%.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/2bddf7ad-b8a0-4aa4-a81e-7e062a2af7a7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Four-day skid breaks:** Nasdaq and the S&P 500 each gained 0.8% after the print as the major averages tried to end a four-session losing streak, even with hike bets rising.
* **Odds spiked, then settled:** Markets priced a Sept. 16 increase at 68% before the report, touched 90% after the core miss, then settled near 82%. Polymarket printed 81%.
* **Ten-year tagged 4.98%:** The benchmark yield hit 4.98%, a three-year high, then eased to about 4.92%. The 2-year yield rose to 4.594% after jumping as much as 8.8 basis points.
* **Oil slipped, diesel record:** Brent fell more than 3% but stayed above $104. WTI traded near $100. GasBuddy said the U.S. average diesel price topped $6 a gallon Thursday for the first time.

# [Nvidia CEO: Circular financing? Let's do more of that](https://substack.com/redirect/2bddf7ad-b8a0-4aa4-a81e-7e062a2af7a7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Jensen Huang told a Goldman Sachs conference Thursday that if Nvidia's AI financing looks circular, the company should do more of it, arguing $1 in produces $100 back.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/2bddf7ad-b8a0-4aa4-a81e-7e062a2af7a7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Sure-thing contracts:** Huang said Nvidia can see about $100 billion of contracted customer demand behind projects it helps finance and called the work lined-up contracts and real stuff.
* **Balance-sheet footprint:** Nvidia disclosed $99 billion of equity investments as of July 26 and $25 billion of future commitments, plus a $500 billion infrastructure platform with six firms including BlackRock.
* **OpenAI Ohio backstop:** Nvidia agreed to guarantee up to $105 billion so OpenAI can lease an Ohio data-center campus that will run on its chips; total guarantees could reach $108.5 billion.
* **CoreWeave cash example:** Nvidia invested $2 billion in CoreWeave in January. Huang said the financing strategy builds newer clouds as distribution channels for the company's architecture.
